Nahouri : La police municipale de Pô reçoit un tricycle et du matériel informatique offerts par le groupe Tigayiri
items.description: BURKINA -NAHOURI-DON-MATERIEL Nahouri : La police municipale de Pô reçoit un tricycle et du matériel informatique offerts par le groupe Tigayiri Pô, 5 août 2026 (AIB)-Le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Pô, Ilassa Dianda a réceptionné ce mercredi 5 août 2026, un lot de matériel composé d'un tricycle, deux ordinateurs et une imprimante au profit de la police municipale. Le don estimé à plus de 2 000 000 de F CFA est du Président-directeur général (PDG) du groupe-Tigayiri, Kodjo Pascal Tigayiri. La police municipale de Pô voit ses moyens d'action renforcés ce mercredi 05 août 2026, par la dotation de matériel composé d'un tricycle, deux ordinateurs et une imprimante par le Président-directeur général (PDG) du groupe Tigayiri, Kodjo Pascal Tigayiri, pour faciliter le travail quotidien et le déplacement des agents de la police municipale sur le terrain. Ce don fait suite à une requête formulée par le directeur de la police municipale, le contrôleur de police Léon K. Naguiabou, a été réceptionné par le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Pô, Ilassa Dianda. Le représentant du groupe Tigayiri, Ibrahim Barro a souligné l'importance d'accompagner les autorités locales. « A travers ce geste, notre groupe souhaite apporter sa contribution à la sécurité et au bien-être des populations de Pô. La police municipale joue un rôle essentiel au quotidien, et il était nécessaire pour nous de lui offrir des outils adaptés pour mener à bien ses missions », a-t-il conclu. Après avoir réceptionné le matériel, le PDS a exprimé sa gratitude envers le donateur pour cet acte de citoyenneté et de solidarité. Tout en saluant cet appui logistique précieux, Ilassa Dianda s’est engagé à l'usage des équipements. « Je tiens à rassurer le donateur que ce matériel sera utilisé de manière rationnelle et exclusivement dans le cadre du service, afin d'optimiser l'efficacité de notre police municipale au bénéfice de tous », a-t-il soutenu. Agence d’information du Burkina HKO/HB/OO

items.title: Le Maroc réaffirme à Amman son soutien aux droits légitimes du peuple palestinien
items.description: Le Royaume du Maroc a réaffirmé, mercredi à Amman, son attachement indéfectible et son soutien constant aux droits légitimes du peuple palestinien frère, pour le recouvrement de sa liberté et l’établissement de son État indépendant dans les frontières du 4 juin 1967, avec Al-Qods pour capitale. Rabat a également réitéré sa conviction que le dialogue et les négociations constituent la seule voie pour résoudre le conflit israélo-palestinien, loin de la violence, de l’extrémisme et des actions unilatérales, et réaffirmant son engagement total en faveur de toutes les initiatives et les efforts visant à atteindre cet objectif. Intervenant au nom du Maroc lors de la réunion ministérielle de soutien à Al-Qods et à ses lieux saints, le ministre de la Justice, Abdellatif Ouahbi, a souligné que l'escalade continue et dangereuse qu’a connue la région au cours de cette année « ne doit pas nous faire oublier notre cause centrale et prioritaire, ni les agressions, les confiscations de terres, les destructions d’habitations et l’expansion des colonies que connaissent les autres territoires palestiniens ». Il a, dans ce sens, relevé que le Royaume du Maroc renouvelle son appel à mettre fin à toutes les pratiques et agressions visant le peuple palestinien en Cisjordanie et dans la bande de Gaza, et à œuvrer à l’ouverture d’un horizon politique clair permettant de mettre fin à ce conflit. Le ministre a également insisté sur la nécessité de soutenir la Ville sainte et de renforcer la résilience de ses habitants afin de leur permettre de faire face aux défis de cette période difficile, mettant en lumière les efforts déployés par le Royaume, conformément aux hautes instructions du Roi Mohammed VI, Président du Comité Al-Qods, et grâce au suivi personnel du Souverain qui ne cesse de multiplier sans relâche ses efforts, ses démarches diplomatiques et ses initiatives concrètes sur le terrain, à travers les projets et programmes économiques, sociaux et culturels mis en œuvre par l’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif, bras exécutif du Comité Al-Qods, au profit des populations locales, dans le but de préserver le cachet civilisationnel authentique de la Ville sainte et de protéger son statut juridique. Dans ce sillage, Ouahbi a réaffirmé l’attachement du Royaume du Maroc à l’importance du rôle de la tutelle hachémite assumée par le Roi Abdallah II Ibn Al Hussein de Jordanie, dans la protection des lieux saints islamiques et chrétiens de la ville d’Al-Qods. Il a en outre indiqué que le Royaume du Maroc, sous la conduite du Roi Mohammed VI, Président du Comité Al-Qods, n’a eu de cesse d’insister sur la nécessité de s’abstenir de tout acte susceptible d’attiser la situation dans les territoires palestiniens, mettant en garde que l’escalade constatée au cours des derniers mois à Al-Qods et à la Mosquée Al-Aqsa, tant sur le plan juridique que sur le terrain, dans un contexte d’instrumentalisation inacceptable des tensions que connaît la région, augure d'une aggravation des tensions et de l’escalade, sur fond de la montée de l’extrémisme religieux et de propagation du discours de haine. Le ministre a ajouté que la situation qui sévit, depuis plusieurs mois, dans la ville d’Al-Qods Acharif et l’enceinte de la Mosquée Al-Aqsa constitue un indicateur fort d’une orientation irrationnelle et contraire au droit, qui compromet les accords en vigueur jusqu’à présent visant à préserver la ville d’Al-Qods et ses lieux de culte face aux agendas politiques locaux et régionaux. Ouahbi a, d'autre part, fait noter que cette réunion ministérielle se tient dans un contexte particulièrement grave que traversent la cause palestinienne et Al-Qods Acharif, en particulier, en raison des incursions, attaques et agressions sans précédent contre la Mosquée Al-Aqsa, ainsi que des actes d’intimidation visant les fidèles, sous la protection des forces israéliennes et sous divers prétextes. Et d'enchaîner que ces agressions ont été accompagnées, sur le plan juridique, par de nombreuses mesures visant à porter atteinte à l’identité de la Ville Sainte, et à effacer ses caractéristiques civilisationnelles et religieuses, avec à leur tête la Mosquée Al-Aqsa. Il a, à ce propos, insisté sur le fait que toute atteinte au statut juridique en vigueur dans la ville d’Al-Qods et dans l’enceinte sacrée d’Al-Haram Al-Qodsi, ainsi que les tentatives d’imposer une division temporelle et spatiale de la Mosquée Al-Aqsa et d’en faire une réalité quotidienne, sont totalement rejetées et doivent cesser immédiatement, dans l’intérêt de la paix et de la stabilité dans la région. A noter que le Maroc était représenté à cette réunion ministérielle par une délégation conduite par Abdellatif Ouahbi, composée notamment de l'ambassadeur du Maroc à Amman, Fouad Akhrif, du directeur des Affaires maghrébines, arabes et islamiques au ministère des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Marocains résidant à l’étranger, Khalid Bencheikh. The post Le Maroc réaffirme à Amman son soutien aux droits légitimes du peuple palestinien appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Dangote Refinery drops PMS to ₦1,165/Litre, Diesel to ₦1,570/Litre
items.description: Dangote Petroleum Refinery has announced a reduction in the ex-depot prices of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) and Automotive Gas Oil (Diesel), effective Thursday 6th of August, thereby reaffirming its commitment to providing affordable, high-quality petroleum products to the Nigerian market. Under the new pricing structure, the refinery has reduced the ex-depot price of PMS to N1,165 per litre, down from N1,215 per litre, representing a reduction of N50 per litre. Similarly, the ex-depot price of Diesel has been reduced to N1,570 per litre from N1,650 per litre, amounting to a decrease of N80 per litre. The price review reflects Dangote Refinery’s ongoing efforts to enhance energy affordability, improve access to refined petroleum products, and support economic activities across Nigeria. The refinery remains committed to ensuring stable supply while leveraging operational efficiencies to deliver value to consumers, businesses, and stakeholders. As Africa’s largest refinery, Dangote Petroleum Refinery continues to play a pivotal role in strengthening Nigeria’s energy security, reducing reliance on imports, and supporting the nation’s economic development through the supply of world-class petroleum products. The company reaffirmed its dedication to contributing to the growth of the Nigerian economy and passing on the benefits of improved operational efficiencies to consumers whenever market conditions permit. items.title: Some domestic airlines may go extinct in 30 days – Onyema
items.description: …faults unions’ interference in ticket sales charge issue By Dickson Omobola Vice Chairman of Airline Operators of Nigeria, AON, Allen Onyema, Wednesday, warned that many domestic airlines may go out of business within the next 30 days unless Federal Government urgently addresses the challenges confronting the aviation industry. Onyema, also the Chairman of Nigeria’s largest airline, Air Peace, cautioned aviation unions against picketing any airline over the five per cent Ticket Sales Charge, TSC, saying if the unions do so, other domestic carriers would suspend operations. He spoke at the launch of the book: ‘Pathways, Pilgrimage & Destiny: The Biography of Alhaji Muneer Bankole,’ unveiled in Lagos in honour of the Chief Executive Officer of the defunct Med-View Airline, Alhaji Muneer Bankole. Lauding Bankole for his contributions to the aviation sector, he said: “Going into aviation is not a piece of cake. It is an industry that is not very rewarding. It is capital intensive, yet less rewarding. Today, we are facing a phase that has existential threats except something drastic is done very quickly within the next 30 days, a lot of airlines might go extinct.” On the unions’ planned action to picket airlines over the unremittance of the TSC, he said: “The Nigerian airline industry doesn’t have any problem with any union, nor do we have business with the unions. This is an aberration; it has never been heard before. If we have problems with the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, we discuss. Whenever they call us, we answer them. “The airlines in Nigeria are operating under very excruciating circumstances. Even the International Air Transport Association, IATA, has said it is very difficult for any airline to survive in this country. Nevertheless, we are treating this kind of statement from IATA with kid gloves. “Everybody pities Nigerian airlines, yet nobody wants to do anything about their situation. Take a look at the mortality rate of airlines in Nigeria. Is anybody addressing it? Over 50 airlines have come and gone. The owners of these airlines succeeded in other businesses, yet they failed in airline business. Why not do self-introspection? Why are these airlines failing? If they (unions) want to shut down the industry, we are waiting for them. “If they picket any airline, others will go because there’s no need for that. There is nowhere in the world that government agencies use unions to talk about issues of debt. These airlines borrow money at 30, 33 percent. All everybody wants is to collect money from airlines. Nobody cares about the lives of these airlines. If they want to shut down the industry, we are waiting for them. “It is not only the five per cent TSC that is hurting the airlines. There are other charges, and we pay for everything we do. Maybe we should think of a solution to bring this to an end. Airlines do not want to owe. There should be a solution on how to go about making it work for everybody. You might think of a unit cost, and even announce that everybody using the Nigerian airline to fly anywhere, this is a unit cost. “The airlines are not against helping government generate revenue. But no airline in the world is taxed directly for revenue. The airlines indirectly provide revenue for government. Those who are sponsoring unions to bring airlines down, we wish them well. At a time the whole world is supporting airlines. At a time every country is trying to inject money to their airlines because of the Iran war, Nigeria is trying to do the other things wrong.” Meanwhile, Mr Bankole, in his remarks, said: “When you look at the title of the biography: Pathways, Pilgrimage & Destiny, it reflects the journey I have gone through in my life. I have been privileged to travel the paths that have shaped my lifetime. The pathways represent the routes I have taken. The pilgrimage symbolises life’s journey, one in which we often do not know the exact destination. We are born, we live, and every day unfolds according to God’s direction. When you wake up in the morning, it is only God who directs your steps for that day. That is the honest message I want to share with all of you. When you go to sleep at night, you know nothing about what the next day holds. It is only when day breaks that you begin another stage of your life’s journey. That journey began for me in 1956. Nigeria Airways, for those of you who grew up in this country, was one of the best airlines. “If anybody has any doubt about it, we have some people that we called first level. They flew aircraft from Lagos all the way to New York. Non-stop. Three times, four times a week. I am proud to have been trained. That was a wonderful period I went through in my life.” The post Some domestic airlines may go extinct in 30 days – Onyema appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Alger : vidéo choc d’une tentative d’agression d’un imam dans une mosquée, 2 suspects arrêtés
items.description: La violence urbaine prend des proportions inquiétantes à Alger. Lors d’une bagarre à l’arme blanche entre des bandes rivales à Bordj el Kiffan, deux personnes ont tenté d’agresser un imam dans une mosquée. La scène a été filmée et la vidéo diffusée sur les réseaux sociaux. Les images font froid dans le dos, puisque jusque-là, les mosquées étaient épargnées par les rixes urbaines. Ce mercredi, la Sûreté de la wilaya d’Alger a annoncé l’arrestation de deux suspects pour « profanation d'une mosquée et tentative d'agression contre l'imam ». Interpellés la semaine passée, ils sont soupçonnés de faire partie d’un gang de quartier qui « terrorisait les habitants », et se « livrait à des rixes de rue à l'aide d'armes blanches prohibées ». Vidéo choquante d’une rixe et d’une tentative d’agression d’un imam dans une mosquée à Alger L'affaire a débuté après la découverte, par les enquêteurs, d'une vidéo circulant sur les réseaux sociaux montrant deux individus se battant dans la rue avec des armes blanches prohibées. Ensuite, ils ont tenté d’agresser un imam dans une mosquée de Bordj El Kiffan. Six armes blanches prohibées de types et de tailles variés ont également été saisies et les deux suspects ont été déférés devant le parquet régional compétent. Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a déclaré lundi 27 juillet que l’Algérie menait une « guerre acharnée contre les bandes de quartier ». items.title: Three foreigners injured in South Africa anti-migrant march
items.description: Three foreign nationals were injured in South Africa on Wednesday when a protest against undocumented migrants turned violent, police in KwaZulu-Natal said. KwaZulu-Natal has been the epicentre of long-running demonstrations against irregular migration, which has already left four foreigners dead and seen African governments repatriate their citizens. Police said the three sustained injuries when protesters began looting shops in Kranskop, some 150 kilometres (93 miles) from the eastern city of Durban. “Two of the injured victims are receiving medical attention at a hospital, whereas the third victim is yet to be located,” a statement read. “Preliminary investigations indicate that the victims are in the country legally, however their immigration status will be verified.” Their nationality was not given. Groups campaigning against undocumented migrants set a June 30 deadline for them to leave the country. Tensions and intimidation have forced more than 176,000 people to flee, according to an AFP tally based on figures released by African governments that have repatriated their nationals. Police said at least 80 people were arrested in Kranskop. One of the three victims was reportedly robbed of cash, they added. Amnesty International on Tuesday called on the South African authorities to “stop vigilante groups that are unlawfully targeting migrants, business owners and communities”. Shenilla Mohamed, the rights monitor’s executive director for South Africa, said the government in Pretoria had failed to act decisively against those behind the protests. “Although the government has made it clear that it will not tolerate illegal identity checks, acts of intimidation and vigilante behaviour, such abuses are still taking place,” she added. “Authorities must move beyond statements of concern and demonstrate through effective investigations, prosecutions and accountability measures that no person or group is above the law.” AFP The post Three foreigners injured in South Africa anti-migrant march appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: We’ve started paying depositors of 46 microfinance banks — NDIC
items.description: …Over 700,000 Heritage Bank depositors paid By Cynthia Alo The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation, NDIC, has said that it commenced payment of depositors of the 46 microfinance banks whose operating licences were revoked by the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, in July. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NDIC, Mr. Thompson Sunday, disclosed this on Wednesday during an interview with journalists at the 2026 stakeholders’ retreat for members of the House of Representatives Committee on Insurance and Actuarial Matters in Lagos. The retreat was held under the theme, “Strengthening Financial Safety Nets in an Era of Banking Sector Recapitalisation and Fintech Innovation.” Recall that last month, CBN revoked the operating licences of 46 microfinance banks following their failure to meet regulatory requirements. The affected banks were found to have inadequate assets to meet their liabilities, ceased operations without regulatory approval, stopped financial intermediation, failed to commence operations within 12 months of obtaining their licences or failed to maintain the required minimum capital base unimpaired by losses. Speaking on the development, Sunday said NDIC, which was appointed provisional liquidator following the revocation, had started paying guaranteed deposits to affected customers. He said: “The CBN revoked the licenses, and we became appointed as the provisional liquidator. We have started paying depositors of those banks, and gradually, we intend to cover all the insured depositors. “Our function as liquidator would involve payment of guaranteed sums. Thereafter, what we do is we go after those who are owing the institutions and have not paid. “We also make sure that we sell the assets that are available and also realise their investment towards paying the uninsured portion of the deposit.” Sunday explained that NDIC was now working with the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System, NIBSS, to identify alternative accounts linked to depositors’ Bank Verification Numbers, BVNs, and make payments automatically. He said: “Hitherto, we used to depend on people to come file for payment, but now, in collaboration with the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System, what we do is, for every account that has a BVN, we trace your alternative account in other institutions and make payments to you automatically. “So, the more we discover those, the more we start payment.” The NDIC boss said the same process had been used in the payment of verified depositors of the defunct Heritage Bank, adding that about 700,000 depositors had so far been reimbursed. He said insured deposits were paid in less than four days after the bank’s failure, while liquidation dividends were subsequently declared for depositors with balances above the insured limit. Sunday said some Heritage Bank depositors who could not be traced through available databases still needed to come forward with evidence of account ownership and other relevant documents for verification. He said: “For the guaranteed sum, we do not need you to come to be paid. Of course, there are challenges in the Nigerian system. “There are depositors that we have not been able to trace, and this is an opportunity for them to also come forward.” He added that more than 98 per cent of depositors, representing over 281 million accounts across insured institutions, were fully covered by the NDIC deposit insurance scheme. Sunday also disclosed that following the revocation of the licences of Aso Savings and Union Homes Savings and Loans banks, insured depositors were paid within 72 hours, compared with the statutory 30-day requirement and the seven-day international benchmark. He said NDIC was pursuing recovery of debts owed to the failed institutions and selling their assets to raise funds for depositors whose balances exceed the insured amount. “Again, the uninsured portion, I’ll still tell you, we need to go after those who have borrowed from those institutions and refused to pay, and also we need to sell the assets. “So, if you look at our website, sometimes on the pages of newspapers, even through electronic media, we advertise properties for sale. It is all towards making sure that we get money to pay the uninsured portions of the deposit,” he said. items.title: Vacances universitaires : Seule l’entrée principale sur l’avenue Thomas Sankara sera ouverte à l’Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo jusqu’au 1er octobre
items.description: Dans un communiqué publié ce mercredi 5 août 2026, le président de l’Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo (UJKZ), le Pr Antoine Béré, a informé la communauté universitaire de l’entrée en vigueur d’une nouvelle réglementation des entrées et sorties sur le campus de Zogona. Cette mesure s’applique du 31 juillet au 1er octobre 2026. Les vacances universitaires ayant officiellement débuté le 31 juillet, l'Université a jugé nécessaire d’adapter l’accès à son site principal. La nouvelle disposition concerne l’ensemble des usagers : enseignants-chercheurs, personnels administratifs, techniques et de soutien (ATOS), étudiants, prestataires et partenaires de l’institution. Pendant cette période du 1er août au 1er octobre, plusieurs portes d’entrée resteront fermées. Seule la porte principale, située au sud du campus le long du boulevard Thomas Sankara, demeurera ouverte en continu, 24h/24, pour garantir un accès permanent au site. Le président de l’UJKZ invite les usagers à prendre leurs dispositions afin d’éviter tout désagrément lié à cette réorganisation. Il précise que cette décision a été prise dans l’intérêt supérieur de la communauté universitaire. Le Pr Béré a adressé ses vœux d’excellentes vacances à l’ensemble des membres de la communauté et les a appelé à respecter scrupuleusement cette nouvelle réglementation, gage d’une application efficace et sereine. items.title: House Committee, NDIC move to strengthen safety net for depositors
items.description: By Cynthia Alo Following the completion of bank recapitalisation exercise, the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) and the House of Representatives Committee on Insurance and Actuarial Matters have moved to strengthen Nigeria’s financial safety net to ensure prompt protection of depositors in the event of bank failures. The move came as over 60 members of the House committee met with the NDIC, Wednesday, in Lagos to examine the implications of the recapitalisation exercise, and growing risks associated with fintech innovation. Speaking at the stakeholders’ retreat with the theme, “Strengthening the Financial Safety Net in an Era of Banking Sector Recapitalisation and Fintech Innovation, Chairman of the committee, Ahmadu Jaha, said stronger bank capital must be matched with stronger supervision and effective depositor protection. He said: “Stronger capital, however, must be complemented by stronger supervision, effective deposit insurance, sound corporate governance, enhanced crisis management arrangements, and improved coordination among members of the financial safety net.” Jaha said the rapid expansion of financial technology had also created new risks requiring continuous legislative attention. “Equally important is the rapid expansion of financial technology. While fintech innovation has significantly increased financial inclusion and payment efficiency, it also raises complex issues relating to cyber resilience, operational risk, consumer protection, digital fraud, and the scope of deposit insurance coverage,” he added. Jaha, who represents Chibok, Damboa and Gwoza Federal Constituency, said lawmakers would provide legislative support and oversight to strengthen implementation of the banking sector recapitalisation programme. He said the committee would also ensure that financial institutions lived up to expectations under the new recapitalisation policy. According to him, the retreat was aimed at helping lawmakers understand the role of NDIC as one of Nigeria’s financial safety-net institutions, particularly in protecting depositors when banks fail. “Whenever there is a failure in banking, that particular safety net mechanism can be applied immediately, and depositors can get their money as at when due,” he said. Also speaking at the event,Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NDIC, Mr. Thompson Sunday, noted that the conclusion of the recapitalisation exercise on March 31, 2026, must be followed by stronger risk management, governance, and compliance across the industry. “While recapitalisation enhances the resilience of financial institutions, it must be complemented by effective regulation, sound governance practices, strong risk management frameworks and good compliance culture, all attribute of a reliable financial safety net.” Sunday said a strong and well-coordinated financial safety net was necessary to maintain public confidence, protect depositors and support orderly resolution of distressed financial institutions. He added that NDIC would ensure prompt reimbursement of insured deposits when bank failures occurred and facilitate recovery of assets for uninsured depositors, creditors and shareholders. He emphasized that NDIC relies heavily on the National Assembly to strengthen the legal framework supporting its core mandates, which include deposit insurance, bank liquidation, prudential regulation, and failure resolution. “Our Act gives us four mandates, right? We do deposit guarantee or insurance, we do bank liquidation, we do prudential regulation and supervision with the CBN, and we also do failure resolution. Now, to do this, we depend on the committees of the National Assembly that have oversight powers over us,” he added. The NDIC boss also said fintech growth had expanded financial inclusion but created new risks, including cyber threats, fraud, data breaches and operational vulnerabilities. He said NDIC would continue to work with the CBN and other regulators to identify emerging risks and strengthen the resilience of the financial system. items.title: La SNDE numérise ses services à travers la plateforme « Khidmaty »
items.description: La Société nationale de l'eau a lancé ses nouveaux services numériques après les avoir reliés au portail national des services publics « Khidmaty », dans le cadre d'une initiative visant, selon elle, à simplifier les démarches administratives et à permettre aux citoyens d'accéder aux services de la société par voie électronique. Ce projet permet aux clients de la société de bénéficier d’un ensemble de services numériques via le portail « Khidmati », ce qui réduit les délais d’accès aux services, facilite leur utilisation et limite les démarches traditionnelles, dans le cadre de la politique nationale de numérisation des services publics. Le lancement de ces services s’inscrit, selon les informations communiquées, dans le cadre d’un programme gouvernemental visant à accélérer la transformation numérique, à améliorer la qualité des services publics et à optimiser l’expérience utilisateur, grâce à l’adoption de solutions numériques modernes adaptées aux exigences de l’administration contemporaine. Ce projet est le fruit d’une collaboration entre le ministère de la Transformation numérique et de la Modernisation de l’administration et l’Agence allemande de coopération internationale (GIZ), visant à soutenir le processus de numérisation en Mauritanie et à étendre la portée des services en ligne, ce qui contribue à rapprocher l’administration des citoyens et à renforcer l’efficacité des services publics.

items.title: South Africa plans new rules on ex-leaders’ foreign trips after Zuma’s visit to India
items.description: South Africa’s foreign minister wants new rules and “more transparency” to apply to former heads of state undertaking foreign trips. The recommendation to parliament follows a controversial visit to India last month by ex-President Jacob Zuma where he met one of the businessmen allegedly at the heart of a huge corruption scandal that played a role in bringing down his government. The uproar over his meeting with Ajay Gupta prompted one minister to say that Zuma was showing the “middle finger” to South Africa. Around a decade ago, the Gupta brothers were accused of profiting from their close links to then-President Zuma and influencing South African policy. Both parties denied wrongdoing. The Gupta family left South Africa in 2018 after a judicial commission began investigating allegations they were involved in massive fraud, known as “state capture”. In 2022, the commission concluded that Zuma had hired and fired ministers central to the running of the country’s economy at the behest of the Gupta family. The South African authorities ended up cancelling their arrest warrant for Ajay Gupta. The two younger Gupta brothers, Atul and Rajesh, went to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where a court in 2023 turned down a South African request to extradite them Zuma has since been expelled from the African National Congress (ANC), the party he once led, and now heads the opposition uMkhonto we Sizwe (MK). During Zuma’s visit to India, a photograph of the 84-year-old South African politician and Ajay Gupta was taken at an Indian temple. South Africa’s high commissioner to India, Anil Sooklal, was also pictured with the duo and he has since been recalled. The diplomat has denied any wrongdoing. Foreign Affairs Minister Ronald Lamola said that his department had submitted a recommendation to parliament and the president’s office for new protocols for former heads of state during foreign trips. They would have to “provide full details” on the upcoming trip for “an informed assessment of the appropriate level of support required and any associated reputational, political, diplomatic or security risks”, he said at a briefing on Wednesday. This is not the first time Zuma’s foreign visits have caused controversy. Last year, he visited Morocco and spoke in support of the North African nation’s claim over the disputed territory of Western Sahara – something South Africa opposes. Zuma undertook the trip as MK leader but was pictured in front of the South African flag when he met Morocco’s foreign minister and brought up Western Sahara. South Africa condemned the visit and raised a formal diplomatic protest about it with Morocco.

items.title: Just In: 176 victims abducted in Kwara released – State govt
items.description: Kwara State Government has confirmed that all victims abducted during the February 3, 2026 attack on Woro and Nuku communities in Kaiama Local Government Area have regained their freedom. The state government announced this on Wednesday through a post on its Facebook page, ending months of uncertainty over the fate of the 176 residents taken away during the deadly assault. The government wrote, “Woro kidnap victims regain freedom. Alihamdulillaah and kudos to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR, security forces, and everyone who played a role in this huge feat. We are grateful!” The victims were kidnapped after suspected Boko Haram-linked extremists reportedly invaded the rural communities on motorcycles and carried out a coordinated attack that lasted several hours. Reports at the time indicated that more than 200 people were killed, several others sustained injuries, homes and businesses were destroyed, and many residents fled the affected communities. Local vigilantes who attempted to resist the attackers were said to have been overwhelmed, with some allegedly trapped and burnt inside their office during the assault. As of the time of filing this report, the state government had not disclosed further details about the circumstances of the victims’ release, including whether any rescue operation, negotiation, or other intervention led to their freedom. items.description: La Société mauritanienne des hydrocarbures (SMH) et la société Cosmos Energy ont examiné les moyens d'accélérer la mise en œuvre des différentes phases de développement du projet gazier « Tortue Ahmeyime Grand » (GTA) et de renforcer leur coopération afin d'améliorer la performance économique du projet et d'optimiser ses retombées. Cette rencontre a eu lieu lors de la réception, par le directeur général de la Société mauritanienne des hydrocarbures, Mohamed Lemine Ould Raqani, d’une délégation de haut niveau de Cosmos Energy, présidée par le premier vice-président chargé des affaires extérieures, William Tuttle, et à laquelle participaient le premier vice-président responsable des activités de la société en Mauritanie et au Sénégal, Todd Nebrogi, ainsi que le vice-président et directeur de la société en Mauritanie, Ismail Sid Ahmed. Selon un communiqué de la société, la rencontre a porté sur l’état d’avancement des principaux dossiers liés au développement du projet GTA, en mettant l’accent sur les mesures susceptibles d’accélérer la mise en œuvre de ses différentes phases, d’améliorer ses performances opérationnelles et de renforcer la valeur économique qu’il apporte à la Mauritanie et aux partenaires du projet. Les deux parties ont réaffirmé leur engagement à poursuivre leur coordination et leur collaboration afin de garantir la mise en œuvre du projet conformément aux objectifs fixés, celui-ci étant considéré comme l’un des projets gaziers les plus importants de la région et un pilier essentiel du renforcement du secteur énergétique et du soutien au développement économique en Mauritanie.

items.title: Edo PDP faction rejects Aziegbemi’s comments on party leadership
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — A faction of the Edo State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has rejected comments by Dr. Tony Aziegbemi on the party’s leadership, insisting he is not the recognised chairman of the party in the state. The development follows Aziegbemi’s criticism of Hon. Austin Nwachukwu, who addressed a recent press conference as Chairman of the Forum of PDP State Chairmen. In a statement circulated on social media, Aziegbemi questioned Nwachukwu’s status, alleging that he had been suspended in October 2025. He also said he was nominated as chairman of the forum at a meeting and argued that the party’s leadership dispute remains before the courts, adding that Taminu Turaki, SAN, should not be described as an expelled member of the PDP. However, in a statement signed by its chairman and secretary, Nosa Ogieva-Okunbor and Chief Hilary Otsu, the Edo PDP faction dismissed Aziegbemi’s position, stating that he lacks the authority to speak on behalf of the party in the state. The statement urged party members, the media and the public to disregard Aziegbemi’s comments. It also declared the faction’s support for the position presented by Nwachukwu, whom it recognised as Chairman of the Forum of PDP State Chairmen. According to the statement, the forum’s position reflects a commitment to constitutional order, party discipline, internal democracy and the preservation of the PDP’s integrity. The faction maintained that the PDP is governed by its constitution, established procedures and the rule of law, stressing that adherence to due process is essential to safeguarding the party’s integrity. It called on party members in Edo State and across the country to remain calm and focused amid the ongoing leadership dispute. items.title: Pakistan, Iran agree to keep border crossings open round the clock to boost trade
items.description: Pakistan and Iran on Wednesday agreed to further expand trade ties by keeping border crossings open round the clock, improving logistics and harmonising customs procedures. The development came during a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and a six-member Iranian delegation, led by Iran’s Minister for Industry, Mine and Trade Mohammad Atabak, in Islamabad, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). During the meeting, the prime minister said that Pakistan highly valued its relations with its close, brotherly neighbour Iran, the PMO said. “Pakistan will continue its sincere efforts for peace in the region,” PM Shehbaz was quoted as saying. He added that he had recently held a productive discussion with Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian on establishing lasting peace in the region and further enhancing Pakistan-Iran bilateral relations, particularly in trade, the statement said. During the meeting, the prime minister expressed hope that sustained efforts would enable both countries to achieve the bilateral trade target of $10 billion set by their leadership, it added. “Both countries will benefit from increased trade, particularly in food, agricultural commodities and related products,” PM Shehbaz said. According to the statement, the meeting also agreed to promote border trade between Pakistan and Iran by expanding facilities to keep border crossings open 24 hours a day. “Both sides also agreed to enhance cooperation in the mining sector, particularly in the processing and value addition of precious stones,” it stated. The Iranian minister said he was grateful to Pakistan for the warm welcome and excellent hospitality. He praised the Pakistani leadership and people for their “sincere diplomatic efforts for regional peace and their expression of solidarity with Iran,” the statement said. “Iran is keen to further expand its economic and trade relations with Pakistan,” Atabak was quoted as saying. “Technical-level negotiations on a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) between Pakistan and Iran are currently underway,” he added. On Tuesday, both countries also reiterated their resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10 billion. In April, Pakistan’s commerce ministry had notified six transit routes for the transportation of goods to Iran via Pakistani sea ports in Gwadar and Karachi. The development had come amid reports that thousands of containers destined for Iran are awaiting clearance at Pakistani ports. Since March this year, both countries have rolled out a series of measures to facilitate border trade, including easing customs procedures, formalising Taftan as a customs station, and notifying new transit routes, against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran conflict in the Middle East that has strained economies in the region and beyond.

items.title: Kano police arrest five over alleged unauthorised distribution of local medicine
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested five suspects over the alleged unauthorised administration and distribution of locally made medicine in the state. The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Wednesday, saying the suspects were arrested following complaints from residents. According to him, operatives of the 52 Police Mobile Force (PMF), Challawa, intercepted six male suspects attached to the Brother Paul Legacy Foundation at the ECWA Church behind the 52 PMF Base in Challawa at about 9:00 a.m. on Tuesday. Kiyawa said the suspects, led by Simon Gbaaondo, 50, from Karu, Nasarawa State, were allegedly administering unverified and unauthorised locally made medicine to a large number of people from the Panshekara community. He alleged that the suspects were administering the medicine free of charge and offering it for sale without clearance from the relevant health regulatory agencies. “The suspects were administering unverified and unauthorised locally made medicine free of charge and also offering it for sale without clearance from the relevant health regulatory agencies. The person who hosted them on the church premises has also been invited to assist with the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the activity,” Kiyawa said. The PPRO said the case was initially reported at the Panshekara Police Division before being transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (CID), where five suspects are currently under investigation. He warned individuals and organisations against conducting medical outreaches or administering drugs and locally made medicine without approval from the Kano State Government, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) and other relevant health authorities. “Individuals and organisations should not administer drugs, locally made medicine or conduct medical outreaches without due authorisation and verification from the state government, NAFDAC and other relevant health authorities. Such acts pose serious health and security risks to the public, especially when large crowds are involved,” he said. Kiyawa added that the command would not tolerate activities capable of endangering public health or disrupting public order. He urged residents to report any suspicious medical outreach or distribution of unverified medicines to the nearest police station. items.title: FG orders payment of civil servants’ outstanding wage award before August 15
items.description: *40% allowance, promotion arrears to be paid later *Last-minute deal saves FG from Labour showdown By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Federal Government has directed that the outstanding two-month wage award owed to federal civil servants be paid on or before August 15, 2026, following a high-level meeting between the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, and the leadership of the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC. The breakthrough, reached at the last minute, effectively averted a planned labour confrontation after the JNPSNC suspended its August 11 ultimatum issued to the Minister’s office over unresolved workers’ welfare issues. The meeting, held on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, was personally chaired by the Minister and attended by the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Finance (Accounts), the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Finance (Special Duties), the Chief of Staff to the Minister, directors, special advisers and other senior officials of the ministry. The labour delegation was led by Comrade Kabiru Ado, National President of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) and National Deputy President of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), who represented the National Chairman of the JNPSNC. Also in attendance were the National Secretary of the JNPSNC and General Secretary of the Nigeria Civil Service Union (NCSU), Comrade Olowoyo Gbenga; the National Assistant Secretary of the JNPSNC and General Secretary of MHWUN, Comrade Kiyawa; and other labour leaders. After extensive deliberations, both parties agreed that the outstanding two-month wage award would be paid on or before August 15. The Minister also assured labour leaders that the Federal Government would facilitate the payment of the long-awaited 40 per cent peculiar allowance through a supplementary budget. According to the resolution, the Ministry of Finance will work with the Budget Office to secure the necessary funding for the allowance. The meeting also revisited the issue of outstanding promotion arrears, with government agreeing that payment processes for batches seven and nine had been resolved. Speaking during the meeting, the Minister emphasized the need for continuous engagement with organised labour to strengthen cordial working relationships with union leaders and ensure timely resolution of workers’ welfare issues. Earlier, Kabiru Ado, who represented the National Chairman of the JNPSNC, Benjamin Anto Uyanto, mni, reassured the Minister of the council’s commitment to protecting workers’ interests. He said the JNPSNC remained ready “to ensure workers welfare are not subjugated.” In his remarks, the National Secretary of the JNPSNC, Olowoyo Gbenga, said the intervention of the union leadership was aimed at preventing an industrial crisis. He said, “The action of the National leadership of JNPSNC was to prevent National embarrassment to the Federal Government because workers were ready to occupy the Office of the Honourable Minister spontaneously.” He further urged government officials and agencies to honour agreements reached with workers and improve communication with labour unions. According to him, “Government officials and agencies of government should always implement decisions and promises to workers without any collapse in communication channels to avoid insinuations.” He also explained the reason behind the ultimatum earlier issued to the Minister’s office, saying, “The inability of the Honourable Minister of Finance office to respond to our various correspondences led to the ultimatum issued to the Honourable Minister’s office.” Speaking after the meeting, Olowoyo announced that the August 11 ultimatum had been suspended following the agreements reached with the government. He said, “With the successful meeting with the Honourable Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, the ultimatum of August 11th issued ab initio has been suspended.” However, he warned that organised labour would closely monitor the implementation of the resolutions reached at the meeting. According to him, “The leadership of JNPSNC, Trade Union Side, will monitor the implementation of our resolutions at the meeting; any iota of failed implementation, workers will not hesitate to picket the Office of the Honourable Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of Economy without any ultimatum.” The post FG orders payment of civil servants’ outstanding wage award before August 15 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigéria : la présidence décide une importante augmentation de salaires pour les militaires atteignant 80% pour les soldats
items.description: La présidence nigériane a décidé d'augmenter les salaires des militaires, avec des hausses pouvant atteindre 80 % pour les simples soldats et 30 % pour les hauts gradés. La présidence a indiqué que cette augmentation entrerait en vigueur à partir du mois de septembre prochain, précisant qu'elle ferait passer le budget de l'armée de 485 millions de dollars à 678 millions de dollars. Cette augmentation et ces mesures d'incitation financière interviennent alors que le Nigeria est confronté à une recrudescence sans précédent des attaques menées par des groupes armés affiliés à Al-Qaïda et à l’État islamique en Afrique de l’Ouest, ainsi qu’à une intensification des activités des bandes de brigands qui se livrent à l’enlèvement d’enfants et de femmes en échange d’une rançon pour leur libération. Le gouvernement nigérian a souligné que cette augmentation des salaires s’inscrit dans le cadre d’un programme de réforme militaire plus large lancé par le gouvernement du président Bola Ahmed Tinubu, qui comprend l’acquisition de matériel et d’équipements militaires modernes, ainsi que l’annonce faite par le président, en juillet dernier, d’une augmentation des effectifs des forces armées. Tinubu a approuvé le renforcement des effectifs de l’armée de 28 000 soldats, une mesure qui, selon le gouvernement, vise à améliorer la préparation des forces armées et à leur permettre de remplir leurs missions et de faire face efficacement aux menaces sécuritaires. Les gouvernements successifs du Nigeria rencontrent des difficultés à endiguer les menaces sécuritaires et l’insécurité dans le nord et le nord-ouest du pays, malgré un déploiement accru de l’armée et une hausse des dépenses militaires, alors que les groupes armés poursuivent leurs attaques contre les forces régulières et continuent d’intimider les populations locales. Le président Bola Ahmed Tinubu a déclaré que son administration accordait la priorité au bien-être des soldats et à la fourniture aux forces armées des armes et des technologies nécessaires pour faire face aux menaces sécuritaires.

items.title: Ga Mantse pledges support for Ghana Medical Trust Fund to improve specialised healthcare access
items.description: The Ga Mantse, His Royal Majesty Nii Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, has pledged his full support for the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF), describing the initiative as a critical national intervention capable of expanding access to specialised healthcare and restoring hope to thousands of Ghanaians living with chronic and life-threatening illnesses. The pledge was made when the Administrator of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, led a delegation, including Board Member Dr Adu Agyei Gyamfi and members of the Fund’s management team, on a courtesy call to the Ga Mantse Palace ahead of this year’s Homowo Festival. The visit formed part of the Fund’s engagement with traditional authorities to strengthen partnerships, raise public awareness and mobilise support for its mission of ensuring that no Ghanaian is denied life-saving specialised healthcare because of financial constraints. During the meeting, the delegation updated the Ga Mantse on the Fund’s progress, its growing impact on patients across the country and its long-term plans to improve access to specialised treatment while investing in healthcare infrastructure, medical equipment, specialist training and research. Welcoming the delegation, the Ga Mantse commended the establishment of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, describing it as one of the country’s most significant healthcare interventions in recent years. He stressed that the health of citizens remains central to national development and pledged to use the influence of the Ga State to promote the Fund’s work. His Royal Majesty also called on Ghanaians, corporate organisations and development partners to support the initiative to enable more patients to receive the specialised medical care they need.

items.title: Chamber of Mines donates GH¢2m relief items to flood victims
items.description: The Ghana Chamber of Mines has donated relief items valued at about GH¢2 million to the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) to support victims of the June 29 floods and other natural disasters. The items, presented at the NADMO headquarters in Accra yesterday, included 1,500 mattresses, 1,500 blankets, 100 cartons of baby food, bags of rice, maize, gari, sugar , beans, bottles of cooking oil, 1,000 pairs of Wellington boots, gloves, detergents, disinfectants and bleach to support NADMO’s operations. Presenting the items, the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Chamber of Mines, Kenneth Ashigbey, said the donation was intended to provide relief and comfort to families affected by the floods as they worked to rebuild their lives. He expressed condolence to families who lost relatives in the disaster and said the chamber stood in solidarity with all those whose homes, businesses and livelihoods had been destroyed. Responsible mining Mr Ashigbey said the donation also reflected the chamber’s commitment to responsible mining and corporate citizenship. He explained that responsible mining went beyond extracting minerals to investing in people, supporting communities and standing with the nation during difficult times. He commended member companies of the chamber for contributing to the donation despite some of them also being affected by the floods. Mr Ashigbey said while the heavy rains contributed to the flooding, human activities had worsened the impact of the disaster, citing illegal mining, construction in watercourses and wetlands, poor waste disposal and disregard for engineering advice as factors that had increased the country’s vulnerability to flooding. “Nature delivered the rains, but human beings multiplied the disaster,” he said, adding that the country must ensure that illegal mining, destruction of wetlands and unauthorised developments in flood-prone areas were not allowed to continue. Commendation Receiving the items on behalf of the government, the Deputy Minister for the Interior, Ebenezer Telarbi, commended the Chamber of Mines and its member companies for the timely intervention. He said the flooding was a personal tragedy for many families whose homes, livelihoods and loved ones had been lost, and that the donation would provide immediate support to affected households. Mr Telarbi assured the chamber that the relief items would be distributed fairly and transparently to those most in need. “The relief items being presented today may not replace everything that you have lost, but they represent something equally important — hope, compassion and solidarity,” he said. He urged other corporate organisations, faith-based institutions and philanthropists to support the ongoing relief and recovery efforts, as disaster management was a shared responsibility. The deputy minister also called for stronger disaster preparedness through proper physical planning, improved drainage systems, protection of watercourses, responsible waste management and strict enforcement of development regulations in flood-prone areas.

items.title: NCCE empowers student leaders to champion integrity, accountability
items.description: The Ashanti Regional Directorate of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) has empowered student leaders from selected tertiary institutions in the Ashanti Region to promote integrity, accountability, and the rule of law within their campuses and communities. The initiative forms part of a Youth Leaders’ Empowerment Dialogue Session organised under the Participation, Accountability, and Integrity for a Resilient Democracy (PAIReD) Programme. The PAIReD Programme is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-financed by the European Union (EU) and the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance. The dialogue brought together more than 65 student leaders from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED), Garden City University, and Kumasi Technical University (KsTU). Participants included executives and members of Civic Education Clubs, Student Representative Councils (SRCs), and other organised youth groups committed to promoting responsible leadership on their respective campuses. Madam Akua Zakaria, Deputy Ashanti Regional Director of the NCCE, opening the session, underscored the critical role of young leaders in shaping positive attitudes and strengthening democratic governance. She urged the participants to use their leadership positions to promote integrity, accountability, and responsible citizenship among their peers. Madam Zakaria said respect for the 1992 Constitution and the laws of Ghana remained fundamental to sustaining democratic governance and national development. She encouraged the students to uphold justice, fairness, and equality in their leadership while rejecting corruption and other practices that undermined public trust and development. Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Godwin Ahianyo, Public Relations Officer of the Ashanti Regional Police Command, took participants through the Whistleblower Act, 2006 (Act 720), and the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989). He explained the legal protections available to whistleblowers, the procedures for requesting information from public institutions, and the significance of the two laws in promoting transparency, accountability, and active citizen participation in governance. Evans Nunoo, a Deputy Director of the NCCE, who spoke on ethical leadership and conflict of interest, urged the student leaders to demonstrate honesty, transparency, and selfless service in the discharge of their responsibilities. He advised them to avoid situations that could create conflicts between their personal interests and their leadership responsibilities, stressing the need to place public interest above personal gain. The participants later engaged resource persons in an interactive discussion on practical strategies for promoting integrity, accountability, and ethical leadership within their institutions.

items.title: Aba residents, businesses count losses over two-week power outage
items.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Residents and business owners in Aba, covering the nine local government areas of the Ukwa Ngwa zone of Abia State, have lamented the power outage that has persisted for more than two weeks, saying it has adversely affected their lives and businesses. Geometric Power Aba Limited (GPAL), the operator of the Aba Ring-fenced Area, has been unable to supply electricity to the city for the past two weeks due to what it described as an inability to source gas from its supplier. Residents and business operators who spoke to Vanguard said they had been counting their losses since the outage began. An eatery operator in the Umungasi area of Aba North, who identified himself simply as Jerry, said he might soon be forced to shut down his businesses because of the rising cost of maintaining alternative power sources. He said he spends about ₦50,000 daily to power the two restaurants he operates in Umungasi and Ogbor Hill. According to him, the high cost of fuel, running the businesses, paying staff and meeting family responsibilities has become overwhelming. “I’m afraid my businesses will soon fold up because of the high cost of maintaining alternative power supply since the outage began. Fuel now sells for about ₦1,300 per litre. I pay my staff, procure items for my business and cater for my family and dependants. How can I make a profit? It is no longer easy. The outage is affecting my business negatively,” he said. An ice and sachet water producer also told Vanguard that she had suspended production pending the restoration of electricity, saying she could no longer afford the cost of running her generating set. Another resident, Mrs. Ngozi Nwankwo, said the prolonged blackout had placed additional financial pressure on her family. She explained that her household could no longer cope with the high cost of fuel needed to power their refrigerator and preserve food items. Some residents called on the Federal Government to grant a licence to another electricity company to supply power to Aba. Meanwhile, Chairman of Geometric Power, Prof. Barth Nnaji, attributed the outage to a disruption in gas supply. Speaking during a fact-finding visit by members of the Abia State House of Assembly, Nnaji explained that the company’s gas supplier, Heirs Energy, had reported the failure of the clutch gear and starter motor at its Associated Gas Gathering Plant in Obigbo, Rivers State, due to ageing equipment. Apologising to residents and businesses for the disruption, Nnaji urged the Federal Government to address gas supply challenges affecting the power sector, noting that about 73 per cent of Nigeria’s electricity is generated from gas-fired power plants. “Nigeria cannot be among the six countries with the largest natural gas reserves in the world and still be experiencing recurring gas-related power crises,” he said. The post Aba residents, businesses count losses over two-week power outage appeared first on Vanguard News .

As part of the donation, the Ghana Medical Trust Fund presented 100 boxes of bottled water and 100 boxes of assorted soft drinks to support activities marking the annual traditional festival. Receiving the items, the Ga Mantse expressed appreciation to the Fund for the gesture, describing it as a demonstration of respect for Ghana’s cultural heritage and traditions. He commended the Ghana Medical Trust Fund for combining its healthcare mission with efforts to support important national and cultural events, noting that such partnerships strengthen the bond between traditional institutions and national development initiatives. The donation formed part of the Trust Fund’s broader engagement with traditional leaders across the country to deepen collaboration, increase awareness of its interventions and strengthen support for improving access to specialised healthcare for Ghanaians.

items.title: Consommation abusive des produits psychoactifs : Le gouvernement appelle à la responsabilité face à une menace de santé publique
items.description: Lomé, 5 août (ATOP) – Face à la consommation abusive de boissons énergisantes, de liqueurs artisanales vendues en dehors de tout contrôle sanitaire, de substances de diverses natures ainsi que l’usage détourné de médicaments psychoactifs, constituant une véritable menace pour la santé publique, le ministère chargé de la Santé a, à travers un communiqué, rendu public le mercredi 5 août, appelle à la responsabilité de chacun. Ces pratiques, souvent banalisées, indique le communiqué, détruisent progressivement l’organisme. Elles fragilisent le cœur, le foie, les reins et le cerveau. Elles favorisent l’apparition de maladies chroniques, réduisent l’espérance de vie et compromettent l’avenir des plus jeunes notamment. Le communiqué précise également qu’au-delà de la souffrance humaine, les conséquences de ces comportements représentent un coût économique et social considérable pour les familles et la nation entière. « Préserver sa santé est aussi un acte de patriotisme. C’est protéger sa famille, contribuer au développement du pays et permettre à notre système de santé de continuer à répondre efficacement aux besoins de tous », souligne le ministre en charge de la Santé, Jean-Marie Koffi Tessi. Par ailleurs, le ministre invite la jeunesse à pratiquer régulièrement une activité physique ; privilégier l’eau comme principale boisson d’hydratation ; adopter une alimentation saine en consommant davantage de fruits et légumes locaux et à prendre moins de sucre, de sel et d’huile. Il conseille également d’éviter la prise de substances nocives ou de médicaments en dehors d’une prescription médicale et de rechercher le bien-être dans un mode de vie équilibré. « Notre santé n’a pas de prix. Nous l’entretenons au quotidien par des choix et des habitudes responsables. Ensemble, faisons de la prévention le premier médicament, et de la responsabilité individuelle le premier rempart contre la maladie », martèle le ministre. ATOP/BA/Communiqué du ministère de la Santé

items.title: Education Ministry condemns Obuasi SHTS violence, directs GES to investigate assault on headmaster
items.description: The Ministry of Education has directed the Ghana Education Service (GES) to investigate the violent disturbance at Obuasi Senior High Technical School that left the school’s headmaster injured and ensure that persons found culpable face appropriate sanctions. The Ministry described the attack on Headmaster Abdulai Zakaria as “reprehensible and criminal”, insisting that acts of violence have no place in Ghana’s educational institutions. In a statement signed by Deputy Minister for Education, Dr Clement Abas Apak, the Ministry said the incident must be thoroughly investigated and addressed in line with existing education sector regulations. “The Ministry considers this act of violence and lawlessness as reprehensible and criminal. Such conduct has no place within Ghana’s educational institutions and will not be tolerated under any circumstances,” the statement said. Headmaster Zakaria was rushed to the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) in Kumasi after he was allegedly assaulted by students during unrest on the school campus on Tuesday night. Obuasi Municipal Chief Executive Faustilove Appiah Kannin confirmed that the headmaster was first admitted at the AngloGold Ashanti Hospital in Obuasi before being transferred to KATH for further treatment. “He has a fracture in the head. And that is why he has been rushed to Komfo Anokye,” she said in an interview on Asaase Breakfast Show. The Ghana Police Service intervened to restore calm at the school, with officers remaining deployed on campus to maintain security. Some students were also arrested in connection with the disturbance. The Education Ministry said the Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, has instructed the GES to immediately commence a full investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. The Ministry added that it will work with the GES and other relevant state institutions to strengthen discipline, protect school leaders and students, and ensure schools remain safe environments for teaching and learning. Meanwhile, authorities in Obuasi are assessing the security situation at the school as discussions continue whether students should be temporarily sent home. The Municipal Chief Executive said a possible closure of the school is being considered, although no final decision has been taken. The exact circumstances that triggered the unrest remain unclear, while police investigations into the incident continue.

items.title: Police arrest another suspect over killing of UNIJOS graduate Ibrahim Mbaya
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa Jos — The Plateau State Police Command has arrested another suspect in connection with the alleged mob killing of University of Jos graduate, Ibrahim Mbaya, as investigations into the incident continue. The Command described the arrest as a significant breakthrough in its ongoing investigation into the death of Mbaya, whose alleged torture by a mob following accusations of theft sparked widespread public outrage. The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Alfred Alabo, disclosed this in a statement issued on Wednesday in Jos. According to the statement, detectives acting on credible intelligence arrested Yusuf Christopher Beskeni, 24, over his alleged involvement in the incident. The police said preliminary investigations indicate that the suspect allegedly participated in the assault on the deceased. According to the statement, the suspect is alleged to have helped tie Mbaya to a pole while he was assaulted by members of the mob. “The suspect allegedly played an active role in the unlawful assault on the deceased. He is specifically alleged to have participated in tying the deceased to a pole while he was subjected to severe assault by members of the mob,” the statement said. The Command said the suspect is in custody and assisting with the investigation, while efforts have been intensified to apprehend other suspects still at large. The Acting Commissioner of Police in Plateau State, DCP Usman Sheikh Adamu, assured the family of the deceased and residents of the state that the Command remains committed to ensuring that everyone found culpable is brought to justice. He said no effort would be spared in investigating the case and prosecuting those found responsible in accordance with the law. The police also appealed to members of the public with useful information to assist ongoing investigations by reporting to the nearest police formation. The Command reaffirmed its commitment to protecting the rights of citizens and ensuring justice is served. Mbaya, popularly known as “Ibee,” died on July 27 after he was allegedly assaulted by a mob over accusations of stealing a mobile phone at an off-campus residence in Jos. The incident triggered widespread condemnation and renewed calls for an end to mob justice. With the latest arrest, the number of suspects in police custody has risen to five, while investigations and efforts to apprehend other fleeing suspects continue. items.title: Sweet scent of Ghana has gone afar: Toronto is a testament
items.description: One would not want to speak for other cities around the world where our countrymen and women have found a home; however, from what I tasted of Toronto in Canada a few weeks back, the sweet aroma of Ghana was literally everywhere. Shocked beyond belief by some of the brief encounters I had had, plus what I was hearing, I decided to pick some areas to visit to back up my experience. Since the 2026 FIFA World Cup had just commenced, Ghana had just played its maiden match against Panama, securing a sweet victory at the Toronto stadium. The excitement of the victory was all over. I could not help but get a feel of the stadium where it all happened. I visited, and what a double sweet aroma I got. Sankofa Square Near the stadium is the strategically located, newly inaugurated “Sankofa” Square, which was unveiled by Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, Asantehene, just before the opening match against Panama. As described to me by some who attended, the extraordinary display of Ghanaian culture was witnessed by over 5,000 people, including Canadian dignitaries, tourists, Ghanaians in the diaspora, business leaders, and football enthusiasts. The gathering apparently turned out to be a celebration of Ghanaian heritage, as Otumfuo and his entourage of Ashanti chiefs sat in state to receive guests. As the Square, formerly known as Yonge-Dundas Square in downtown Toronto, gave way to “Sankofa”, a Twi word which, when literally translated, means going back (to one’s roots), it is no taboo. Whoever might have selected the name and, with the blessings of the Toronto city authorities, hit the nail on the head. Additionally, the Asantehene coming down to inaugurate the renamed Square makes one even more delighted. The presence of Ghana in downtown Toronto has remained since that historic day, and the aroma will linger. Scents of Ghana Toronto, well and truly, has all the scents of Ghana, which qualifies it to be an extension of Ghana with the representations that transcend most aspects of our rich culture back home. It took me all the way to a Toronto local eatery to learn that the food, Tuo Zaafi, is also known as “Diehuo”. I had never heard of that name as the alternative for tuo zafi in Accra, where I have lived for most of my life. Having been presented with the menu at the eatery, in ignorance, I asked embarrassingly what “diehuo” was. Genuinely, I had never heard the expression used anywhere. On the menu list featured foods like fried yam with tilapia and fresh pepper, waakye with garri and macaroni, banku and okro stew, fufu, jollof rice and kokonte, which I was told was the favourite of the many who patronise the place. I was even told someone cooks and sells Hausa koko with all the accompaniments somewhere in the area. During a drive around the market shops, I discovered market names such as New Asafo market, Kantamanto market, Makola, Central market, and Adepa market. In all those markets, Twi seems to be the lingua franca, as one could hear transactions and conversations that went on. On sale were fresh yams from Ghana, Koobi, cocoyam, apem, Zomi red oil, smoked fish and many other food items one could find in Kaneshie market back in Accra. Interestingly, one shop I visited had then just taken delivery of fresh apem and koobi from Ghana that morning. At the Ghanaian Presbyterian Church of Toronto, where I joined worship one Sunday, the atmosphere was no different from that of my regular church back home. They projected the Presbyterian hymns in both Twi and Ga. Their worship songs were mostly the kind one is used to back home, and the dance steps were no different. Most of the worshippers were proudly dressed in their Ghanaian attire, with modern styles. After the beautiful Church service, I checked in at their book stall. In a corner, on display, were some Ghanaian newspapers, including “The Ghanaian News”. I picked a copy to read. About 60 per cent of the 56-page newspaper had news from Ghana, which was quite helpful. The rest was on Toronto news with a lot of advertising. Through the newspaper, I learned that there were many Ghanaian professionals in the Toronto area who had set up consultancy services, from health care to legal assistance, finance and tax, insurance, shipping and cargo, as well as world travel and tours. It was encouraging to note that Ghanaian professionals in Canada are doing well on the surface. Old student reunions also found space in the newspaper, and so did the power-packed herbal Bitters prepared with multiple herbs. As they advertise back home, those Bitters heal thousands of different diseases, from low sperm count to fibroid, diabetes, hypertension and infertility. At the end of my visit, I concluded that Toronto is a perfect Ghanaian settlement. One can walk through there and feel very much as if one were on Ghanaian soil. The gaping differences are their good roads, schools, health provision, cleanliness, environmental consciousness and responsible attitudes. Otherwise, the sweet scents of Ghana very much prevail in the cosmopolitan city of Toronto. ****** The writer can be contacted via email: vickywirekoandoh@yahoo.com
