items.title: Sebta et Melilla : de l’autre côté, l’illusion
items.description: Les événements tragiques survenus aux abords de Sebta et Melilla appellent d’abord au recueillement et au respect dû aux victimes et à leurs familles. Mais l’émotion, aussi légitime soit-elle, doit également laisser place à l’analyse. Lorsque des jeunes sont prêts à mettre leur vie en danger pour franchir une frontière, nous sommes confrontés à un phénomène qui dépasse la seule question migratoire et qui mérite une réflexion collective à la hauteur de sa gravité. Dans ces circonstances particulièrement difficiles, l’État marocain a assumé pleinement ses responsabilités. Les autorités publiques ont été mobilisées pour préserver l’ordre public, protéger les personnes et les biens et assurer le retour des citoyens, dans le cadre d’une coordination avec les autorités espagnoles. L’ouverture d’enquêtes par les autorités judiciaires compétentes participe de cette même logique : celle d’un État qui dispose d’institutions solides, agit dans le cadre de la loi et entend faire toute la lumière sur les circonstances de tels événements. Cette réalité mérite d’être rappelée au moment où certaines lectures étrangères semblent parfois oublier la responsabilité considérable assumée par le Maroc dans la gestion des flux migratoires aux frontières méridionales de l’Europe. Notre pays est devenu, au fil des années, un partenaire incontournable dans la lutte contre l’immigration irrégulière, les réseaux criminels et la traite des êtres humains. Il serait pour le moins injuste de réduire cet engagement à quelques images ou à des analyses étrangères parfois privées de la complexité nécessaire. Mais précisément parce que le Maroc dispose d’un État solide et d’institutions capables de faire face aux situations les plus complexes, nous pouvons porter la réflexion au-delà de l’urgence. Les événements de Sebta et Melilla doivent nous conduire à nous interroger sur les ressorts qui permettent aux réseaux criminels et aux marchands d’illusions de convaincre certains jeunes que leur avenir se trouverait nécessairement ailleurs. Cette interrogation intervient alors même que le Maroc connaît l’une des transformations les plus importantes de son histoire contemporaine. Sous la conduite de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, le Royaume a changé d’échelle. Tanger Med, l’essor des industries automobile et aéronautique, les infrastructures ferroviaires et autoroutières, les énergies renouvelables, l’attractivité croissante du Royaume, son ancrage africain et les avancées diplomatiques majeures enregistrées sur la question de notre intégrité territoriale témoignent d’une trajectoire que peu de pays comparables ont été capables d'accomplir en un temps aussi court. L’enjeu consiste désormais à prolonger cette dynamique en faisant de la jeunesse l’un des principaux bénéficiaires et acteurs de cette transformation. L’emploi, la qualité de l’enseignement et de la formation, l’entrepreneuriat, la mobilité sociale et la justice territoriale constituent à cet égard des priorités déterminantes. Il ne s’agit pas de remettre en cause le chemin parcouru, mais au contraire de s’appuyer sur les acquis considérables du Royaume pour ouvrir une nouvelle étape de son développement. La justice territoriale revêt ici une importance particulière. Les opportunités économiques, l’accès à une formation de qualité, le financement de l’initiative ou les possibilités d’entreprendre doivent continuer à se diffuser dans l’ensemble des régions. C’est aussi par cette diffusion des opportunités que se consolident la cohésion nationale et la confiance. À l’approche des prochaines élections législatives, cette question mérite d’occuper une place centrale dans le débat démocratique. Les échéances électorales ne sont pas seulement des moments de compétition politique ; elles permettent de fixer les priorités d’un nouveau cycle d’action publique. Emploi, formation, entrepreneuriat, développement territorial et participation des jeunes doivent pouvoir se traduire en politiques concrètes, déclinées aussi bien à l’échelle nationale que régionale et locale. Mais il serait erroné de considérer que tout relève de l’État. La solidité de l’État marocain ne dispense aucun autre acteur de ses responsabilités. Les entreprises ont un rôle dans l’emploi et la formation, les partis dans la représentation et le renouvellement des élites, les collectivités dans le développement territorial, l’école et l’université dans la transmission des compétences, les médias dans la qualité du débat public, et les familles comme la société civile dans l’accompagnement des nouvelles générations. La jeunesse est une responsabilité nationale, donc nécessairement collective. Cette mobilisation doit également concerner l’espace numérique. Les trafiquants d’êtres humains et les réseaux criminels ont appris à exploiter les frustrations, les rumeurs et les mécanismes de viralité des plateformes. Quelques vidéos, de fausses informations ou la promesse mensongère d’un passage facile peuvent suffire à provoquer des comportements dramatiques. Protéger la jeunesse contre ces manipulations relève désormais autant de la prévention que de la sécurité. Enfin, notre capacité à examiner ces événements ne doit jamais être confondue avec une quelconque complaisance envers ceux qui cherchent à les instrumentaliser contre le Maroc. Un pays sûr de ses institutions peut analyser ses difficultés sans accepter qu’elles servent de prétexte au dénigrement de son action, de son image ou, plus encore, de ses intérêts fondamentaux et de son intégrité territoriale. Les événements de Sebta et Melilla doivent ainsi constituer un moment de mobilisation nationale. Le Maroc dispose aujourd’hui d’acquis économiques, institutionnels et diplomatiques considérables. Sa stabilité, la continuité de ses choix stratégiques et la vision portée par Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI lui ont permis de franchir des étapes décisives. L’enjeu est désormais de mettre pleinement cette puissance acquise au service d’une ambition simple : offrir à la jeunesse marocaine suffisamment d’opportunités, de mobilité sociale et de perspectives pour que ceux qui cherchent à lui vendre l’illusion d’un avenir ailleurs ne trouvent plus de terrain sur lequel prospérer. The post Sebta et Melilla : de l’autre côté, l’illusion appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Transport fares to remain unchanged as operators’ welcome gov’t fuel price intervention
items.description: The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) and the Ghana Road Transport Coordinating Council (GRTCC) have announced that transport fares will remain unchanged across the country, following the government’s recent intervention to reduce diesel prices. In a press release issued on Wednesday, August 5, the transport operators welcomed the government’s decision to reduce the regulatory margin on diesel by GH¢2.00 per litre for a one-month period, describing the move as a timely response to concerns raised by the transport sector. The union said they had engaged the sector minister prior to the intervention, advocating for relief for commercial drivers in the face of rising operational costs. “We are happy that those engagements yielded results. We welcome these measures and urge government to extend the current window beyond one month should oil prices continue to rise,” the statement said. Read also: Transport operators, gov’t meet today over proposed 30% fare increase Following consultations with their national executives and key stakeholders, the GPRTU and GRTCC announced that transport fares will remain unchanged across all routes until further notice. The operators also directed drivers, station masters and branch executives to strictly adhere to the approved fare structure, warning against the imposition of unauthorised charges on passengers. “No additional charges outside the official fare table will be permitted. Any commuter required to pay above the approved fare should report the matter immediately to the nearest union office for prompt redress,” the statement added. The unions expressed appreciation to the government, led by President John Dramani Mahama, for the fuel price intervention, which took effect on Tuesday, August 4, 2026, and is expected to remain in force for one month.

items.title: Makinde, Obi fault Nigeria’s leadership, Methodist Church seeks action on insecurity, economy
items.description: By Adeola Badru Ibadan — Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, and the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, on Wednesday said Nigeria’s development challenges stem largely from poor leadership, despite the country’s abundant human and natural resources. The Methodist Church Nigeria also urged the Federal Government to intensify efforts to tackle insecurity, inflation, the depreciation of the naira and the rising cost of living. They spoke at the opening of the Methodist Church Nigeria’s 50th/15th Biennial Conference in Ibadan, Oyo State. The conference, attended by delegates from across Nigeria and the diaspora, is themed “I Will Fight For You” (Exodus 14:14) and focuses on issues of national security, governance, economic recovery, leadership and justice. Governor Makinde commended the Methodist Church for its longstanding contributions to nation-building through evangelism, education, healthcare and community development. He said institutions such as the Church play a vital role in shaping values and strengthening society. “Nations are not built by government alone. They are built by institutions that shape values, strengthen families and inspire hope. The Methodist Church has remained one of those institutions,” he said. The governor also praised the Church for speaking on national issues and holding public office holders accountable. Speaking on leadership, Makinde said those entrusted with public office must pursue justice, peace and equal opportunities for all citizens. “Leadership is not about privilege. It is about responsibility. It is measured not by the promises we make but by the lives we improve,” he said. According to him, while government can provide infrastructure and public services, nation-building ultimately depends on integrity, compassion and shared values. Makinde said his administration had prioritised improving the lives of ordinary citizens rather than focusing on political interests. He maintained that Nigeria’s challenge is not a shortage of talent or resources but the quality of leadership. “Our nation does not lack talent. It does not lack resources. What Nigeria needs now more than ever is leadership that brings people together around a common purpose and the courage to place service above self,” he said. The governor also publicly declared his intention to contest the presidency in the future, saying he would offer leadership focused on service and national development if given the opportunity. Peter Obi, in his address, also attributed Nigeria’s challenges to poor leadership. “There is nothing wrong with Nigeria. The only thing wrong with Nigeria is leadership. We have enough land to cultivate the food we need. We have enough human capital to develop like any nation. We have enough natural resources to generate sufficient revenue,” he said. Obi called for greater investment in agriculture, education and healthcare, stressing that Nigeria must move from consumption to production and value creation. He also urged religious leaders to continue speaking truth to those in authority and advocating good governance. Earlier, the Prelate of Methodist Church Nigeria, His Eminence, Dr. Oliver Ali Aba, called on the Federal Government to strengthen efforts to address insecurity, inflation, the depreciation of the naira and rising energy costs. He described insecurity as a major threat to national development, noting that many farming communities had been adversely affected by banditry, kidnapping and violent attacks. “I call on the Federal Government to rise to one of its primary constitutional responsibilities of securing lives and property,” he said. The Prelate welcomed the recent rescue of schoolchildren, teachers and a principal abducted in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State, while expressing sympathy over the victims who lost their lives during the incident. On the economy, he appealed to the Federal Government to implement measures aimed at reducing inflation, stabilising the naira and easing the cost of living. He also urged leaders at all levels of government to demonstrate accountability and fulfil their responsibilities to the people. The conference continues in Ibadan with delegates expected to deliberate on issues relating to national development, security, economic reforms, moral leadership and the role of the Church in promoting peace, justice and national unity. The post Makinde, Obi fault Nigeria’s leadership, Methodist Church seeks action on insecurity, economy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La brecha en la financiación autonómica se ensancha: Murcia recibe 977 euros menos por habitante que Cantabria
items.description: En pleno debate sobre la reforma del modelo de financiación autonómica , el sistema sigue agrandando las diferencias entre territorios y ha batido un nuevo récord: la brecha de recursos que separa a la comunidad mejor financiada, Cantabria, de la peor, Murcia, se sitúa en máximos históricos. Según un análisis del centro de estudios Fedea, el esquema vigente, que trata de garantizar unos servicios públicos de calidad similar en todo el país, asignó a cada murciano 3.372 euros en 2024 —últimos datos disponibles— para destinar a los servicios públicos básicos, casi un tercio por debajo de lo que recibieron los habitantes de Cantabria. La diferencia es de 977 euros, un 2% más con respecto a los resultados del ejercicio precedente. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Dangote Refinery drops PMS to N1,165/litre, diesel to N1,570/litre
items.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Petroleum Refinery has announced a reduction in the ex-depot prices of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) and Automotive Gas Oil (Diesel), effective Thursday 6th of August, thereby reaffirming its commitment to providing affordable, high-quality petroleum products to the Nigerian market. The company in a statement said, under the new pricing structure, the refinery has reduced the ex-depot price of PMS to N1,165 per litre, down from N1,215 per litre, representing a reduction of N50 per litre. Similarly, the ex-depot price of Diesel has been reduced to N1,570 per litre from N1,650 per litre, amounting to a decrease of N80 per litre. The price review reflects Dangote Refinery’s ongoing efforts to enhance energy affordability, improve access to refined petroleum products, and support economic activities across Nigeria. The refinery remains committed to ensuring stable supply while leveraging operational efficiencies to deliver value to consumers, businesses, and stakeholders. As Africa’s largest refinery, Dangote Petroleum Refinery continues to play a pivotal role in strengthening Nigeria’s energy security, reducing reliance on imports, and supporting the nation’s economic development through the supply of world-class petroleum products. The company reaffirmed its dedication to contributing to the growth of the Nigerian economy and passing on the benefits of improved operational efficiencies to consumers whenever market conditions permit. items.title: StopNCII: Free online tool offers protection against non-consensual sharing of intimate images
items.description: StopNCII (Stop Non-Consensual Intimate Image Abuse) is a free, survivor-centred online tool that helps adults prevent the sharing of intimate images or videos without their consent. Launched in 2021, the platform is operated by the UK-based charity SWGfL (South West Grid for Learning) in partnership with a coalition of global technology companies. The tool uses a “privacy-first” approach called perceptual hashing. Instead of uploading intimate images, the tool creates a unique digital fingerprint (hash) for each image directly on the user’s device. Only this hash is shared securely with participating platforms. If a platform attempts to upload a matching image, the system blocks it. This approach ensures the actual image is never stored or sent, maintaining the user’s privacy and security. How does It work? Using StopNCII involves straightforward steps: Visit: Stop Non-Consensual Intimate Image Abuse | StopNCII.org and create your case by following the prompts. Select Content: Choose the intimate image(s) or video(s) from your device that you want to protect. Create a Hash: The tool creates a unique digital fingerprint (hash) of the content on your device. The actual image or video remains on your device and is not uploaded. Receive a Case Number: Once the hash is generated, you will receive a case number and PIN. You must keep this information safe, as it is not recoverable and is needed to check your case status or withdraw. Prevent Sharing: The hash is shared with all participating companies. If a platform detects a matching hash, it removes the content, preventing it from being shared. Check Progress: You can use your case number anytime to check the progress of your case online. Global reach and recognition The impact and recognition of StopNCII have grown significantly since its launch. By late 2025, the tool was being used to protect approximately 2 million images, supporting over 785,000 cases globally. It has been recognised by regulators like the UK’s Ofcom as a “leading global example” of proactive NCII prevention. The UN Cybercrime Convention now formally includes NCII, and StopNCII is recognised as an innovative solution for prevention. A growing list of major tech companies participates in the initiative, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Threads, X, Microsoft Bing, Snap Inc., and OnlyFans. The initiative is also supported by a global network of 107 NGOs and receives backing from organisations like the UN Office on Drugs and Crime and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children. StopNCII in the Ghanaian context – Sextortion on the rise The urgency of addressing non-consensual intimate image abuse is particularly acute in Ghana. The Cyber Security Authority has reported a dramatic surge in online blackmail and sextortion cases, with financial losses rising nearly fivefold between early 2024 and early 2025. Between January and April 2024, the CSA recorded 155 reported cases with financial losses amounting to GH¢103,663. By the same period in 2025, losses had ballooned to GH¢499,044. The CSA noted that cybercriminals employ increasingly sophisticated methods, including the use of fake social media profiles and encrypted messaging platforms to reduce traceability. Common tactics used by perpetrators According to the CSA, perpetrators typically create fake social media accounts with attractive profile images to lure unsuspecting individuals into romantic or flirtatious interactions. Once trust is established, they initiate explicit video calls or solicit private photos. These sessions are secretly recorded or saved without the victim’s consent. The perpetrators then threaten to release the compromising materials unless a ransom is paid, usually via mobile money. The CSA has warned that paying a ransom does not guarantee the deletion of content, and in many cases, criminals persist with their demands or intensify the threats. Legal protections in Ghana In Ghana, sharing nude pictures or leaking private intimate videos without permission is a serious crime. Under the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), non-consensual sharing of private, sexual photos or videos is illegal, with offenders facing prison sentences starting from one year up to three years or more. For sextortion — threatening to leak nudes to get money or favours — the punishment is much heavier, ranging from 10 to 25 years in prison. Additionally, the law imposes penalties of not less than five years and not more than ten years for the creation, possession or circulation of indecent images of children. Practical advice for Ghanaians The Cyber Security Authority has issued the following recommendations to protect against online blackmail and sextortion: – Avoid accepting friend requests from unknown individuals. – Be wary of online relationships that progress quickly or involve requests for explicit content. – Keep social media accounts private and limit who can view posts. – Never share or store nude images or videos on any device. – Be cautious of unsolicited messages or offers, especially those promising money or business opportunities. For victims: – Immediately cease all communication with the threat actors. – Do not pay any ransom, as it only encourages repeated extortion and does not ensure deletion of the content. – Preserve all evidence, including screenshots, usernames, URLs, messages, and payment requests. – Report the incident to the CSA via its 24-hour helpline by calling or texting 292, sending a message via WhatsApp to 0501603111, or emailing report@csa.gov.gh. – Seek emotional support from trusted family members or professional counsellors.

items.title: Le gardien de but cap-verdien Vozinha s’engage officiellement avec Colo-Colo
items.description: Après avoir quitté Chaves, pensionnaire de la deuxième division portugaise, le gardien international cap-verdien Vozinha s'est officiellement engagé, le mardi 4 août 2026, avec Colo-Colo, selon une annonce faite par le club. À 40 ans, le héros du Cap-Vert lors de la dernière Coupe du monde ouvre un nouveau chapitre de sa carrière en rejoignant l'un des clubs les plus prestigieux du football sud-américain. Le club chilien Colo-Colo a officialisé, le mardi 4 août 2026, la signature du gardien de but cap-verdien Vozinha. Libre après son passage à Chaves, en deuxième division portugaise, le portier de 40 ans débarque au Chili avec l'ambition de mettre son expérience au service d'une formation habituée aux compétitions de haut niveau. Auteur de prestations remarquées avec la sélection du Cap-Vert lors de la dernière Coupe du monde, où il a contribué au parcours historique des Requins Bleus, Vozinha espère désormais relever un nouveau défi sous les couleurs de Colo-Colo. Lors de sa présentation officielle, l'international cap-verdien n'a pas caché son enthousiasme à l'idée de rejoindre le club chilien. «La Coupe du monde a été le plus beau moment de ma carrière de footballeur, mais c’est désormais du passé. Aujourd’hui, être ici pour représenter Colo-Colo, un grand club à l’histoire prestigieuse, représente pour moi le plus beau moment de ma carrière en club», a déclaré Vozinha. Le gardien a confié avoir été sollicité par plusieurs équipes après son départ du Portugal. Toutefois, il affirme que Colo-Colo constituait son choix prioritaire, convaincu par le projet sportif proposé. Son arrivée au Chili marque une nouvelle étape dans une carrière entamée au Cap-Vert avant de se poursuivre sur le continent européen. De son vrai nom Josimar José Évora Dias, le portier continuera d'évoluer sous le nom de Vozinha, après avoir obtenu une autorisation spéciale lui permettant de conserver ce surnom sur son maillot. Une appellation qui revêt pour lui une forte dimension affective et symbolique, en hommage à ses grands-parents. «Si ma grand-mère ou mes grands-parents étaient encore en vie aujourd’hui, je pense qu’ils seraient très fiers. J’espère continuer à honorer les valeurs qu’ils m’ont transmises. Porter ce nom est un bel hommage à leur mémoire», a-t-il déclaré. Accueilli avec ferveur par les supporters dès son arrivée dimanche à Santiago, le gardien a participé mardi à sa première séance d'entraînement avec ses nouveaux coéquipiers. Sauf contretemps, Vozinha pourrait effectuer ses débuts officiels sous les couleurs de Colo-Colo dès dimanche, à l'occasion de la rencontre de championnat face à l'Unión La Calera. En rejoignant Colo-Colo, Vozinha s'offre un nouveau défi dans un championnat réputé du continent sud-américain. Fort de son expérience et de la confiance acquise après son parcours marquant avec le Cap-Vert sur la scène mondiale, le vétéran entend désormais écrire une nouvelle page de sa carrière sous les couleurs du club chilien. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Le gardien de but cap-verdien Vozinha s'engage officiellement avec Colo-Colo est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: The Democrats’ Riskiest Midterm Play
items.description: The Democratic nominee for Montana’s open U.S. Senate seat, Alani Bankhead, has been telling everyone for months that there is no price anyone can pay to keep her name from appearing on the November ballot. “Why is it you are asking me a question I have been asked a thousand times?” she told me on Monday, when I tried to probe her commitment to the race. “There is nothing that is going to force me from the ticket unless God himself tells me to drop out.” The lack of divine intervention has challenged Democratic hopes for a big-sky Senate pickup . As it stands, Bankhead will likely split the state’s ever shrinking number of non-Republicans with an independent candidate, Seth Bodnar, who has raised more money and secured more support from senior party leaders who believe he will caucus with Democrats if he prevails. That all but ensures a win for the Republican candidate, Kurt Alme, which has set off a last-minute scramble to push Bankhead from the race before the August 10 deadline for locking the ballot. The state Democratic Party has been preparing for her to leave the race. A national Democratic polling firm, Global Strategy Group, circulated new polling yesterday arguing that she should drop out. And national Democrats have been calling her, seeking meetings. Bankhead told me that last week former Governor Steve Bullock , a Democrat who has not yet endorsed in the race, called her to ask if she would meet him for coffee. She said she did not respond. “It is a very strange process to be in this position where Alani feels more like the independent than the independent,” Jeri Duran, her communications strategist, told me. Shannon O’Brien, the head of the state party, convened a meeting of its executive board last Thursday to discuss the possibility of leaving the Democratic line on the ballot empty if Bankhead does leave the race. State law says political parties “shall” appoint a replacement if the nominee bows out 85 or more days from an election. State Democratic party bylaws say that the party central committee “shall” call a meeting and “shall” vote on a replacement. The Montana secretary of state, a Republican, says the state party must follow those words and pick a replacement. But Jacquelyn Lopez, the general counsel for the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, attended the meeting to argue that the party would likely win in court if it opted not to replace Bankhead, according to three people familiar with the meeting who were not authorized to speak publicly. Under this plan, the party would gloss over the “shall”s in state law and party rules on the grounds that political parties have the power to interpret their own rules and significant right under the First Amendment to do what they please. Someone in the meeting asked Lopez if the Democratic National Committee would fund the inevitable lawsuits that would result from such a move, the three people said. Lopez answered in the affirmative, all three said, including one who referenced written notes of the meeting made the following day. “There was without a doubt comments made that made everyone think the DNC would pay for it,” one of the people told me. “For everyone after the meeting, there was the gist that we were going to have our bills paid for us.” Lopez, an attorney at the Elias Law Group, told me that she represented the state party and not the DSCC at the meeting. “I did not state that the DNC would fund a lawsuit at any point, and it would be inaccurate to report that,” she told me. She did not respond to follow-up questions. A spokesperson for the DNC, Angelo Fernández Hernández, told me that the national party “has never been approached to pay any legal bills related to candidates dropping out from the election.” A DSCC spokesperson told me the committee was not involved in the meeting. [ Read: One morning of controlled chaos in Maine ] The discussion only deepened suspicions that national Democrats are conspiring against the state’s Democratic candidate in what is emerging as the clumsiest, if not the most catastrophic, political gambit of the 2026 midterms. “It’s pretty wild out here,” Nancy Keenan, a former Montana Democratic Party executive director, told me. “They call it the Wild West—but holy Toledo.” The disappear-the-Democrat electoral strategy—a response to the party’s terrible national brand, especially in states Donald Trump comfortably won—has had more success elsewhere. In Nebraska, Democrats nominated a candidate for Senate who pledged to abandon her campaign to clear the way for an independent, Dan Osborn. In Idaho, the Democratic Senate nominee, David Roth, dropped out last week to make way for the independent Todd Achilles. Yesterday Julian Beaudion, the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate seat in South Dakota, said he would suspend his campaign to protect “the mental and physical safety of my family,” making way for an independent candidate, Brian Bengs. Democrats hoped Montana would follow a similar script to clear the way for Bodnar, a former university administrator and U.S. Army Green Beret, who is running on a moderate Democratic platform with a “both parties are to blame” message. As former Senator Jon Tester put it in a text message to fellow state Democrats about supporting Bodnar, “During my last two races the democratic Party was poison in my attempts to get re-elected.” But that message never filtered down to the Democratic rank and file, a largely populist and freethinking bunch who have watched their state vote for Trump by double digits three times in a row. Party activists have rebelled, saying that there will be downballot repercussions for abandoning the party brand in the premier statewide race this year, and state voters continue to show significant support for Bankhead, a retired Air Force lieutenant colonel and a first-time candidate. Recent Republican and Democratic polling shows Bodnar and Bankhead roughly splitting the non-Alme vote, giving the Republican a significant double-digit lead in a four-way race that also includes a libertarian candidate. The situation has created a last-minute scramble and deepening paranoia on all sides. Days after Bankhead heard from Bullock, Montanans began getting calls from pollsters, first reported by the Washington Reporter , testing a hypothetical scenario in which Bullock replaced both Bodnar and Bankhead, creating a two-person race between Bullock and Alme. The possibility of Bullock running again for Senate, after losing a bid in 2020, has long circulated in the state, and the funding for the poll has not been disclosed. Bullock did not respond to multiple requests for comment. To make matters more complicated, Bankhead won her June 2 primary with significant financial backing from apparent Bodnar allies, according to federal records. They sided with Bankhead over another primary candidate, the fierce Bodnar critic Reilly Neill. The Progressive Vet PAC spent $2.8 million to support Bankhead and oppose Neill. Jason Carroll, a tech entrepreneur and Bodnar donor, gave the group $200,000. The other $2.6 million came from a nonprofit called Contours Inc. that has supported other independent-candidate efforts. Bankhead maintained that she had no ties to the group, and had made no pledge to get out of the race if she won. She has held true to that bargain. The pledges of other Democrats in the state have been a bit more complex. Back in April, O’Brien told me she would “support the Democratic nominee,” and rejected any rumors that the state party was preparing to clear the way for Bodnar. “To my knowledge there is no intention to change the rules to allow for support of anyone else,” she said. State Senate Minority Leader Pat Flowers told me that the idea of secret plotting for a change in rules to allow Democrats to not field a nominee was a “fever dream.” Days after the executive-board meeting last week, O’Brien sent a four-page legal memo from the Elias Law Group to Democrats in the state. The memo acknowledges that the state party’s bylaws instruct the committee to name a replacement candidate if a nominee withdraws. But it went on to argue that if the party tries to replace a candidate and fails, it would likely survive the resulting lawsuit. “The key question,” the document reads, is how the Montana Democratic Party “interprets its own bylaws and whether a failure to appoint a replacement candidate is defensible as a reasonable interpretation of the party’s own rules.” In one scenario, the state party could construe its rules to put forward a “none of the above” option at its nominating meeting. In another scenario, the state party could require qualifications for a replacement candidate that are so stringent that “no available candidate satisfies those requirements.” [ Read: America’s most divided state loves its extremes ] Bankhead has concluded that O’Brien cannot be trusted. “There is only one person in the state Democratic Party that is standing against me, and that is Shannon O’Brien, who has been in Bodnar’s pocket the whole time,” Bankhead told me. O’Brien has previously denied any effort to support Bodnar, but could not be reached for comment for this story. A spokesperson for the state party declined to comment. Bodnar’s campaign, for its part, says he is prepared to win a four-way contest. A super PAC supporting his campaign began running new ads against Bankhead today, asking, “What else don’t we know about Alani Bankhead?” Bankhead and Bodnar met privately in Helena on Friday, according to three people familiar with the meeting. Bankhead asked Bodnar to drop out and transfer his endorsement and money to her, two people said, which he declined to do. Bankhead told me Monday that Bodnar has not made the same request of her. “He said, I would never ask you to drop out , and I said, Great, because I wouldn’t ,” she told me. But both candidates have also made clear that they think the other can’t win, and allies of Bankhead have been calling for Bodnar’s exit. “If there were somebody else who had a pathway to defeat Kurt Alme in this race, I’d step aside in a heartbeat,” Bodnar told supporters in a livestream Monday night. The pressure is likely to only increase over the coming days, testing Bankhead’s resolve. “Nobody can accurately predict any election,” she told me. “If polls mattered, Hillary would have won. If name ID mattered, Bullock would have won. If money mattered, Tester would have won.” When she mentioned the Almighty as the only one who might persuade her to abandon her campaign, I asked how frequently she communicated with God. “I am a person of faith,” she said.

items.title: Wait—The Theme for Your Party Is What , Exactly?
items.description: On a recent Thursday night, I sat among other guests at a house party and listened intently to a PowerPoint presentation about radium. Lauren Pickens, a 25-year-old who lives in the Washington, D.C., area, stood at the front of the room and flipped through slides about the carcinogenic chemical: A century ago, radium was marketed as a miracle. Americans added it to everything—including food and cosmetics. Within years, some had died. “We’re smarter than that these days,” Pickens said, pivoting to raw milk and other questionable substances people are ingesting today. Everyone laughed. The presentation was part of the theme that night. The co-hosts—Pickens and her boyfriend, Luke Brandl—had sent detailed instructions to everyone: “Pick a historically bad decision, from either personal or public memory, and tell us about it in the form of an 8–10 minute presentation.” We’d then vote and crown a winner. One guest discussed the chaotic 1904 Olympic marathon (one runner ate rotten apples and took a nap during the race, yet still managed to place fourth); another rehashed her relationship with an ex in the form of a book report. The party was held at Brandl’s home, which doubles as a museum of sorts to the various parties the couple has hosted. Sticky notes from an “embracing your cringe” party hung on a wall, as did a poster of the 1978 film Starcrash , which people had watched at another themed party—“bad-movie night.” Pickens and Brandl are more ambitious than the average party planner, but their events lean into a common enthusiasm among young partygoers for niche, even absurd, themes. I’ve been collecting examples for weeks: “dress like your favorite Metro stop,” a murder mystery about tech billionaires on a private island, a farewell to Spirit Airlines (“bring the spirit and spirits”). In some circles, hyper-specific party themes are becoming a norm, sometimes a requirement. “Having a coherent theme is more of an expectation now than it was two years ago,” Alexa Jordan, a 25-year-old incoming law student, told me. She’s hosted a spelling-bee birthday party and a cul-de-sac 5K, which entailed running in a circle for more than 65 laps. She estimated that about eight out of every 10 parties she’s invited to now have a theme. In one sense, the appeal of a niche party is simple. Themes are fun, as people discovered long ago. (In 1897, New York City socialites held a costume ball that has been dubbed the “ most ostentatious party in US history .”) Now that friends are only a text message or FaceTime away, though, there’s also a higher bar for what gets people hanging out in person. Wearing a funky costume or presenting on a weird interest gives people “something to talk about,” Samika Lewis, a 25-year-old who also attended the bad-decisions party, told me. Especially at a time when some young adults are turn ing away from alcohol, a wacky party can act as its own kind of social lubricant. “I never really liked bars that much,” Brandl told me. “I always wanted something a little bit different and more creative.” [ Read: Millennials are sick of drinking ] These parties are themselves fueled by social media as much as they are a rebuke of hyper-online culture. The event I attended started the way it ended—on Partiful. The couple had invited everyone through the popular event-planning app. The morning after, Brandl sent a text blast via Partiful, announcing that a presentation on dueling had won. One of the guests added pictures to the app’s shared photo album. Partiful, which was founded in 2019, has become especially integral to the rise of niche party themes. Events can be made public or accessible only to those who are sent the link, which is the setting that the hosts I talked with primarily use. Public events show up on the homepage for anyone to see, allowing the strangest parties to get lots of attention and priming people to get creative with their own themes. If you’re stuck, the app has a feature, “Ask the Party Genie,” that lets you choose a vibe (such as “chill” or “chaos”) to get specific theme ideas. When I tried it out, the genie suggested that I host parties including “make lamps out of non-lamps” and a “Lana del Rage Room.” On Partiful, RSVPs to “niche and high-concept events” grew more than four times from 2024 to 2025, Partiful’s CEO, Shreya Murthy, told me. [ Read: The internet, but for hot people ] On Instagram and TikTok, many recaps of themed parties draw millions of views, which help inspire more niche parties. Jordan, the law student, hosted her spelling-bee bash after a friend sent her an Instagram Reel of a similar event. At the extreme, social-media memes are themselves the theme. Komal Kamdar, a 27-year-old who lives in New York City, attended a party where guests dressed up like Adam Sandler, who has gone viral for his combinations of a baggy graphic T-shirt and shorts. The result is a feedback loop: People get inspiration from Instagram and TikTok. Then they whip up an invitation on Partiful and upload pictures to social media when the party’s over. In some cases, the themes can start to feel forced—more of a performance for some brief attention online than anything else. In D.C., more than 5,000 Partiful users have expressed interest in attending a five-minute “eat an apple with me” event. Normal park picnics have been rebranded as “sit down and touch grass” events. At the party I attended, one guest scrambled to finish making his PowerPoint before the start of the event. And hosts often drop hundreds of dollars on decorations and spend weeks planning to make sure that the theme comes to life. Kamdar said she spends an average of $200 to host a niche party, and has held fewer gatherings because of the cost. Still, any kind of in-person gathering seems better than the alternative. Americans could certainly stand to party more . At its best, a niche party is not about chasing clout, but about actually getting to know people. At the PowerPoint party, guests initially exchanged awkward small talk and nibbled on homemade garlic knots. But once the presentations began, everyone loosened up. By the end, we hardly felt like strangers at all. As I slipped out, at close to midnight, the stragglers were already talking about Pickens and Brandl’s next party. Of course, there would be a theme: Guests would compete in a treasure hunt dressed up as either a Roman or a pirate.

items.title: $4.5bn Oil-Backed Loan: Tinubu is weapon fashioned against Nigeria – Atiku
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has condemned the National Economic Council’s NEC approval of a $4.5 billion refinancing of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company NNPC Limited’s oil-backed loan, describing President Bola Tinubu as a weapon fashioned against Nigeria’s economy. In a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu on Wednesday in Abuja, the Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC said the fresh borrowing was further proof that the administration had mortgaged the country’s future to sustain its fiscal habits. Shaibu quoted Atiku as saying every new oil-backed obligation pushed Nigeria deeper into a cycle where tomorrow’s wealth is sacrificed to finance today’s policy failures. Atiku recalled that only days earlier, the Presidency had responded to his revelation of an unexplained ₦17 trillion crude oil windfall by claiming Nigeria could not fully benefit from soaring international crude prices because future earnings had already been committed to oil-backed foreign loans. “That explanation should have embarrassed any responsible government. Instead, this administration has chosen to double down on the very scandal it sought to justify by approving yet another $4.5 billion refinancing. Rather than breaking free from the chains of oil-backed indebtedness, it is tightening them,” he said. The former Vice President questioned the logic behind the fresh borrowing given the administration’s revenue-boosting measures. He accused the administration of turning Nigeria into a nation permanently living on credit, at the expense of future generations. Atiku argued that the real tragedy lay in the hardship Nigerians had endured without corresponding gains, noting that while the pain is permanent, but the promised gains remain invisible. He said Tinubu’s promise of renewed hope had instead delivered the opposite. “President Tinubu promised renewed hope. What Nigerians have received is renewed debt, renewed hardship and renewed uncertainty. Under his watch, debt has become policy, borrowing has become governance, and mortgaging the future has become the defining philosophy of his administration,” he said. Atiku called on the administration to immediately publish full details of the refinancing arrangement, including its terms, repayment obligations and the volume of crude oil committed under the deal, insisting that Nigerians deserved transparency and a government that protects rather than mortgages the nation’s future. “Nigeria deserves leadership that preserves national assets, not one that continually pledges them to finance an endless cycle of waste, opacity and fiscal irresponsibility”, he declared. The post $4.5bn Oil-Backed Loan: Tinubu is weapon fashioned against Nigeria – Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kaporo : des riverains tirent la sonnette d’alarme face aux conséquences d’un chantier R+12
items.description: Les travaux de construction d’un immeuble R+12 à Kaporo ne laissent pas indifférents les habitants du secteur. Depuis le démarrage du chantier, plusieurs riverains affirment vivre dans l’inquiétude, évoquant des dégâts constatés sur leurs habitations ainsi que des perturbations dans leur vie quotidienne. Fissures sur les murs, bruits incessants, fortes vibrations… Les habitants disent subir les conséquences des activités menées sur le site. Pour certains, la situation représente désormais une menace pour la sécurité des familles installées à proximité. Kadiatou Diallo fait partie des personnes qui se plaignent des effets du chantier. Selon elle, sa maison aurait subi plusieurs dommages depuis le début des travaux. Elle décrit une situation devenue difficile à supporter. « La nuit, on ne dort pas, même le matin. Hier, quand la pluie est venue abondamment, mon enfant était couché dans la chambre et c’est là que quelque chose est tombé sur les tôles. On pensait que c’était le tonnerre, tellement le bruit était fort. C’est une chose dangereuse. Nous vivons dans la peur chaque jour, nous constatons de nouveaux dégâts et nous ne savons plus vers qui nous tourner », témoigne-t-elle. D’après plusieurs habitants rencontrés, des alertes auraient déjà été adressées aux responsables du chantier et aux autorités compétentes, mais leurs inquiétudes seraient restées sans réponse concrète à ce jour. Les riverains demandent notamment la réalisation d’une expertise technique indépendante afin d’évaluer les éventuels impacts des travaux sur les habitations environnantes et de prendre les mesures nécessaires pour éviter une aggravation de la situation. En attendant une intervention, les habitants de Kaporo appellent les autorités à agir rapidement pour garantir leur sécurité, protéger leurs biens et prévenir tout incident majeur. Christine Finda Kamano L’article Kaporo : des riverains tirent la sonnette d’alarme face aux conséquences d’un chantier R+12 est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Osun election: Police deploy 15,000 personnel DIG, AIGs, CPs for August 15 poll
items.description: By Shina Abubakar Osogbo The Nigeria Police Force has warned politicians, security personnel and electoral officials against attempts to manipulate the August 15 governorship election in Osun State, declaring that anyone arrested for serious electoral offences will be transferred to the Force Headquarters in Abuja for investigation and prosecution. The Commissioner of Police in charge of election security in Osun State, CP Samuel Erale Etaifo, gave the warning on Wednesday while addressing journalists and Divisional Police Officers at the Police Officers’ Mess in Osogbo. Etaifo stated that the police would be deploying about 15,000 personnel, including Commissioners of Police, Assistant Inspectors-General of Police (AIGs), Police Mobile Force (PMF) operatives and other specialised units, to guarantee adequate security before, during and after the gubernatorial election. Describing the poll as a federal electoral assignment, the election security commissioner announced that suspects arrested for electoral offences would be moved out of Osun State to prevent interference with investigations and prosecution. “This governorship election is a federal election. Anyone arrested for electoral offences will be taken out of Osun State to the Force Headquarters for further investigation and prosecution. There will be no room for interference,” he declared. He also issued a strong warning to politicians, electoral officials and security personnel against compromising the electoral process, stressing that the Nigeria Police Force would not tolerate vote buying, ballot snatching, violence, voter intimidation or any other form of electoral malpractice. “I want to warn all political actors, security personnel and even INEC officials not to manipulate the election. Anyone found violating the Electoral Act or attempting to undermine the credibility of the process will be held accountable,” he said. Etaifo disclosed that he was mandated by the Inspector-General of Police to restore peace and coordinate security operations across Osun State ahead of the election. According to him, he had already met Governor Ademola Adeleke to brief him on the assignment and reassure the state government of the police’s commitment to a peaceful poll. “The early deployment of security personnel was intended to boost public confidence and encourage voter turnout by eliminating fear and intimidation. “We cannot have a hostile atmosphere and expect to conduct a free and fair election. The early arrival of police personnel is to boost the confidence of the people of Osun State and discourage voter apathy,” he stated. He maintained that the police would remain neutral and professional, promising a level playing field for all political candidates. “Our duty is to guarantee a level playing field for every political actor. Gone are the days when the police were alleged to be partisan. Every political party must have equal opportunity to campaign and participate in the election without intimidation or harassment,” Etaifo said. The police chief equally warned officers deployed for election against compromise or collusion with politicians, saying erring personnel would face disciplinary action. He urged residents to remain law-abiding, cooperate with security agencies and report suspicious activities, assuring that comprehensive security arrangements had been concluded to ensure a peaceful, free and credible governorship election. items.title: Roads blocked, traffic disrupted as PTI holds rally near Karachi Press Club
items.description: KARACHI: The PTI held a protest near the Karachi Press Club (KPC) on Wednesday to mark three years since the imprisonment of party founder Imran Khan and demand his release. The demonstration led to traffic disruptions in the surrounding areas after authorities blocked routes leading to the venue, causing severe congestion and leaving commuters stranded for extended periods. A screenshot showing closed roads in Karachi’s Saddar Town area. — Screengrab from Google Maps A police official, who wished not to be named, said that some PTI workers and leaders were detained near the Press Club. They confirmed that police resorted to tear gas shelling and used baton charges to disperse the demonstrators, adding that after the police action, the road was cleared for traffic in the evening. The PTI in a statement said it staged demonstrations in Karachi, Hyderabad, Mirpurkhas, Nawabshah, Umerkot, Mithi and other parts of Sindh, with participants demanding Imran’s release. In Karachi, the demonstration was led by PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh, Karachi President Raja Azhar, PTI Sindh General Secretary Dr Masroor Sial and Karachi General Secretary Arsalan Khalid. They and other party leaders led workers towards the Karachi Press Club, according to the statement. “However, according to the party, police blocked all routes leading to the Press Club by placing containers and completely sealed the area to stop protesters from reaching the venue,” the statement claimed. “PTI workers later held a peaceful demonstration near Zaibunnisa Street and Fawara Chowk in Saddar. The party alleged that police resorted to tear gas shelling and baton charge against peaceful protesters, leaving several workers injured,” it alleged. PTI demonstrators stage a protest in Karachi’s Saddar Town area on August 5, 2026. — Photo courtesy PTI The PTI alleged that the police arrested more than ten workers in the metropolis, including Sial. The party further claimed that six PTI workers were arrested in Pano Aqil and fifteen workers in Kandhkot, with cases also registered against them. Addressing the protesters, Sheikh demanded the immediate release of Dr Masroor Sial and all detained workers in Karachi, Pano Aqil and Kandhkot, while Raza Azhar said the PTI “formally submitted an application seeking permission for the peaceful protest, yet police still resorted to unlawful use of force”. Sheikh also took to X and claimed that the route to the KPC had been blocked by containers, slamming the PPP government for sealing off the area. “The Karachi Press Club is neither a Red Zone nor a sensitive security area, yet the PPP government has blocked public access and trampled the constitutional right to peaceful assembly,” he wrote. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah took notice of the congestion and issued strict instructions to the Sindh inspector general and the Karachi additional inspector general to restore traffic flow. “Traffic should be cleared from Sadar, Old City Area, MA Jinnah Road and Zainab Market immediately,” he was quoted as saying in a statement from his office. “Additional traffic police personnel should be deployed on the roads and a report should be submitted.” He further ordered that queues of cars on Napier Road, Regal Chowk and Bolton Market should also be cleared. Similarly, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar sought details from the Karachi Traffic deputy inspector general (DIG) on the traffic jams in the city, with a statement from his office saying that the cause behind the disruption should be determined. “District police should help traffic police in clearing the roads and highways,” Lanjar was quoted as saying. “The difficulties faced by citizens should be immediately addressed.” He ordered that traffic police personnel should be stationed on all major arteries and pressure points to manage the flow of traffic, adding that they need to be cleared immediately to restore traffic flow. “In case of traffic flow being affected, alternative routes should be arranged immediately,” Lanjar added. “Citizens should face minimum difficulties; traffic flow should be ensured at all costs.” Islamabad In Islamabad, the party staged a protest on Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed Road, formerly known as IJP Road, to mark three years since Imran’s imprisonment. The rally was led by PTI Islamabad Regional President Amir Mughal and Regional General Secretary Malik Amir Ali Awan. Mughal told Dawn that it had been decided that only one protest would take place in the federal capital, with Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed Road selected for “a show of power”. Participants chanted slogans and displayed placards highlighting issues including Imran’s imprisonment, the situation in Indian-occupied Kashmir, inflation, unemployment, law and order, and other matters. Hyderabad Similarly, the PTI staged a rally in Hyderabad, but it remained peaceful and no arrests were made by police as witnessed elsewhere. The rally was staged on the joint call of PTI and Tehreek Tahfuz Aayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP) to mark three years of Imran’s imprisonment, starting from Liberty Chowk and culminating outside the local press club. PTI Hyderabad President Mohsin Ghumman, PTI Sindh Deputy General Secretary Arif Ghafoor Sheikh and others attended. The rally remained peaceful, but according to Mohsin Ghumman, police did not allow the demonstrators to set up camps. Police, however, didn’t make any arrests, he confirmed. Activists and workers gathered at Hyder Chowk before reaching the local press club, where they staged a sit-in and played party songs and a recorded clip of Imran’s past speech, amid vociferous slogans. Addressing protesters outside the press club, PTI leaders paid tributes to party workers for their steadfastness. Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023, for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case . While imprisoned, Imran has not met his family or party leaders since his sister Uzma Khanum met him last December, despite a court order from the Islamabad High Court mandating meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays. His sisters have staged regular sit-ins on Tuesdays, demanding meetings with the ex-premier and that he be treated for a severe eye condition. His eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January and he receives government-provided treatment . The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game , with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency in not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and not allowing his personal physicians access to him. The government denies these allegations. The opposition has also demanded that the former premier be shifted to Shifa International Hospital, be treated in the presence of his personal physicians and allowed to meet his family.

items.title: Sedina Tamakloe’s Acquittal: A test of prosecutorial discretion and public confidence in Ghana’s justice system
items.description: The Court of Appeal’s decision on 30 July 2026 to acquit and discharge former Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) Chief Executive Officer, Sedina Tamakloe, has become more than the conclusion of a criminal appeal. It has evolved into a wider debate about prosecutorial discretion, the relationship between the Attorney-General and the appellate courts, the consistency with which the State exercises its powers in politically sensitive cases and the political consequences of the A-G’s decision. Although public discussion has largely centred on the outcome of the appeal, the more enduring constitutional questions arise from the Attorney-General’s immediate, almost unreflective response to the judgment. The Timeline Matters A proper analysis begins with the chronology. Sedina Tamakloe was prosecuted during the administration of President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo. Throughout the trial, many members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) maintained that the prosecution was politically motivated, while the then Attorney-General Godfred Dame insisted it was founded solely on the evidence before the courts. Following her conviction, Tamakloe exercised her constitutional right of appeal. Her Notice of Appeal was filed on 9 May 2024—months before the change of government. The appeal therefore originated under the previous administration and progressed through the normal judicial process, with both the prosecution and defence filing extensive written submissions before the Court of Appeal delivered its judgment. The three-member panel consisted of Justices Emmanuel Ankamah (Presiding), Samuel Obeng-Diawwuo and Emmanuel Senyo Amedahe. Significantly, two members of the panel were appointed during the Akufo-Addo administration, while the third was appointed after the change of government. This composition is relevant because it challenges simplistic attempts by the opposition NPP to portray the judgment as a politically orchestrated decision. Whether one agrees with the Court of Appeal’s reasoning or not, the judgment emerged from an appellate process that began under one administration and was determined by a panel whose appointments spanned two different governments. The law is the law, as they say. The Function of an Appellate Court Every judicial system recognises that trial courts are not infallible. That is precisely why appellate courts exist. Their constitutional responsibility is to review lower court decisions, identify errors of law or procedure where they exist, and correct miscarriages of justice. Every acquittal by an appellate court does not necessarily imply misconduct by a trial judge, just as every conviction does not guarantee the absence of judicial error. Prosecutorial errors at the lower court may lead to aquittal at the appelate court. The appellate process is therefore an integral safeguard within the administration of justice rather than an exception to it. The Attorney-General’s Unreflective Response Public attention shifted almost immediately after the judgment. Within hours of the Court of Appeal’s decision, Attorney-General Dr. Dominic Ayine announced at a press conference that the State intended to appeal to the Supreme Court and would also seek a stay of execution. That was unusual considering the. fact that the case was not prosecuted under the current NDC government, not by A-G Dominic Ayine. Legally, there is nothing extraordinary about the Attorney-General exercising the State’s right of further appeal. Ghana’s legal system expressly permits appeals from the Court of Appeal to the Supreme Court on appropriate legal grounds. But politically, it’s absurd. It makes no sense! The issue that has generated debate is not whether the Attorney-General possesses that authority, but whether the unreflective speed with which the decision was announced against an individual who served in the same government with Dominic Ayine, raises legitimate questions about process, consistency and ulterior motives. For many observers, it appeared unlikely that a detailed appellate judgment of 94 pages could have been fully studied before such a significant public announcement was made. And if it was, why the hurry? Was it meant to keep a woman, a fellow comrade, who is sick and on a wheel chair languishing in prison by all means? Whether that perception is accurate or not, it has contributed to growing public interest in the motives behind the Attorney-General’s decision. Questions of Consistency The controversy has also prompted comparisons with other criminal appeals. In the case of Yaw Appiah, the Court of Appeal recently overturned a conviction after he had spent many years in prison and awarded substantial compensation. Likewise, Yaw Asante Agyekum secured an acquittal after serving a lengthy prison sentence following his conviction for armed robbery with the notorious Atta Ayee. And most famously, the case of Matthew Nyindam, opposition NPP MP for Kpandai who returned to Parliament after the Supreme Court overturned a lower court’s decision affecting his election. In neither case did the Attorney-General pursue a further appeal before the Supreme Court. No two criminal cases are identical, and different legal issues may well justify different prosecutorial decisions. Nevertheless, consistency remains one of the principles by which prosecutorial discretion is often judged. Where similar appellate outcomes receive different responses from the State, questions naturally arise regarding the factors informing those decisions. Such questions do not necessarily imply impropriety; rather, they reflect a legitimate public interest in understanding how prosecutorial discretion is exercised. A-G Dominic Ayine who enjoys addressing the people of Ghana has failed to offer the slightest explanation to these lingering questions from the public, particularly from NDC footsoldiers. The Debate Over a Stay of Execution Perhaps the most contested legal issue concerns the application for a stay of execution following an acquittal. Some legal scholars have argued that once an accused person has been acquitted and discharged by the Court of Appeal, seeking to suspend the effect of that judgment is an exceptional step requiring compelling legal justification. Others maintain that where the State believes the Court of Appeal committed significant errors of law, preserving the status quo pending a final determination by the Supreme Court may be appropriate. Dominic Ayine did not even read the judgement before announcing his intentions. What erroors could the appelate court have made? The differing opinions demonstrate that this is an evolving area of legal interpretation rather than one governed by universally accepted principles. But it is also politically implosive for the NDC. Ultimately, the Supreme Court’s determination may provide much-needed guidance on the circumstances in which such applications should properly be entertained. Law and Politics The case also illustrates the complex relationship between legal decision-making and political perception. Because Sedina Tamakloe previously served under an NDC administration with Dominic Ayine the A-G, some supporters of the governing party have questioned why an Attorney-General appointed by the same government has chosen to pursue the matter so vigorously even without pausing to reflect. Others argue that the Attorney-General’s constitutional duty is owed exclusively to the Republic of Ghana. Under that view, prosecutorial decisions must be based solely on legal merit rather than political affiliation, and neither friendship nor party membership should influence the State’s pursuit of justice. Perhaps those in this school of thought do not live in Ghana otherwise they would know that we are yet to have such an A-G who owes exclusive constitutional duties to the republic.The separation of powers is still a pipe dream. Beyond One Case The Sedina Tamakloe appeal ultimately raises issues extending far beyond one individual’s legal fortunes. It invites broader reflection on the principles guiding prosecutorial discretion, the balance between the independence of the Attorney-General and public accountability, and the relationship between the executive and the judiciary. The Attorney-General is constitutionally entitled to seek the Supreme Court’s review if he believes the Court of Appeal erred in law. Equally, citizens are entitled to understand why that course has been adopted, particularly where comparable appellate decisions appear to have attracted different responses. Did the President of Ghana John Mahama ask his Attorney-General to go after his own former appointee who has been aquitted by the appealate court and to pursue a prosecution at which his opponent failed at the appelate court? In constitutional democracies, public confidence depends not only on the correctness of legal decisions but also on their consistency and transparency. The credibility of the justice system is strengthened when prosecutorial choices are seen to be guided by clear legal principles rather than by considerations that remain unexplained. Dominic Ayine must explain to Ghanaians and redeem his credibility, if there’s any of it left. As this case proceeds before the Supreme Court, the legal outcome will undoubtedly be important. Equally important, however, will be the opportunity for the Attorney-General’s office to articulate the principles that informed its decision. Doing so would contribute not only to the resolution of this case but also to save himself from the wrath of the NDC rank and file. His continues silence only deepens the perception that his unreflective dicision to appeal Sedina’s aquittal is motivated by underhand dealings with opposition elements.

items.title: US lifts sanctions on Iraqi airline linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards
items.description: The United States on Wednesday lifted sanctions targeting Iraq’s Fly Baghdad airline, a company it had previously designated for alleged links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). In an update to its website, the US Treasury lifted sanctions on Fly Baghdad and two of its aircraft, but maintained its sanctions against a man previously identified as the company’s owner, Basheer Abdulkadhim Alwan al-Shabbani. Washington had originally designated the airline, its aircraft and owner in January 2024, alleging that it provided support to the IRGC’s Quds Force and its proxy groups in Iraq, Syria and Lebanon. A US Treasury official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP the airline had been removed after going through the department’s administrative reconsideration process. “FBA (Fly Baghdad Airlines) has demonstrated major changes to their operations such that their listing is no longer warranted,” the official said. They clarified that the removal was “not indicative of any shift in US policy toward the Government of Iran, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps—Qods Force, any designated terrorist organization, or any person who supports or acts on behalf of any of these.” Since US President Donald Trump launched a war against Iran in late February, Washington has killed the country’s top leadership and attempted to cripple its economy with sanctions and military strikes. In retaliation, Tehran has virtually blocked the vital Strait of Hormuz through which about a fifth of the world’s energy supplies normally pass and targeted US allies in the region. Negotiations to end the war have been stop-start, with the status of Iran’s nuclear program and the imposition of potential tolls on the Strait being key sticking points. AFP The post US lifts sanctions on Iraqi airline linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem delivers new Neonatal ICU to transform newborn care in Tarkwa
items.description: AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem Mine has reaffirmed its commitment to improving healthcare in Tarkwa with the commissioning of a modern Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at the Tarkwa Municipal Hospital. This facility replaces an overcrowded makeshift facility that had struggled to meet the needs of critically ill newborns. The new unit, commissioned on July 30, is expected to significantly improve neonatal care in the municipality and neighbouring districts by providing specialised treatment for premature babies and infants with life-threatening conditions. Speaking at the ceremony, Western Regional Health Director, Dr Godfred Sarpong, described the facility as a major step towards reducing preventable newborn deaths in the region. He said many newborn deaths in Ghana remain avoidable and revealed that the Ghana Health Service had recently been tasked to develop strategies to improve neonatal survival. “Every newborn deserves the opportunity to live and live well.” Dr Sarpong said he was particularly encouraged when he learnt that Tarkwa Municipal Hospital was receiving an ultra-modern NICU, describing it as a critical investment that would strengthen newborn care in the Western Region. “This is a huge investment in the lives of our newborns.” He also praised AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem for extending its support beyond mining into healthcare, and urged hospital authorities to maintain the facility so it would continue to serve generations of families. A speech delivered on behalf of the Western Regional Minister, Joseph Nelson, by Rachel Sarpong, also hailed the project as a landmark investment in healthcare delivery and an example of the impact of partnerships between the private sector and public institutions. The Minister’s message described the facility as more than a new hospital block, saying it represents hope for families and a stronger healthcare system. “Today’s event is not merely about commissioning a new healthcare facility; it is about giving hope to families, strengthening our healthcare system and, above all, giving our newborn babies… a better chance at life.” The statement noted that the NICU would reduce avoidable referrals, strengthen the capacity of the Tarkwa Municipal Hospital and improve health outcomes for newborns across the area. It also commended AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem for demonstrating corporate social responsibility through investments that deliver lasting benefits rather than short-term charity, and encouraged other companies to emulate the initiative. Meanwhile, Nana Kweku Twum, leader of the NICU Committee, assured stakeholders that the community would protect and maintain the facility to ensure it continues to serve residents for many years. In recognition of the company’s contribution, he presented a citation to the Managing Director of AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem Mine, Daniel Boadi, in appreciation of the mine’s support. The new NICU marks another milestone in AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem’s investment in community development, with healthcare now joining education and infrastructure as key pillars of the company’s social impact in Tarkwa.

items.title: Rev Stephen Wengam leads first Executive Presbytery mission to The Gambia
items.description: The General Superintendent of Assemblies of God, Ghana, Rev Stephen Wengam, is leading the Executive Presbytery officers of the church on a week- long apostolic and missions visit to The Gambia. Other members of the delegation are Rev Godwin Tito Agyei- Assistant General Superintendent, Rev Ernest Birikorang-General Secretary, Rev Simon Abu Baba- General Treasurer and Rev Dr Freeman Osei- Tete- Head of Operations at the Headquarters of Assemblies of God, Ghana. They were received at the airport in Banjul by a delegation led by the National Head of The Gambia Assemblies of God Mission, Rev Paul Ampofo Williams. Rev Wengam and team will visit various branches of the church in The Gambia. The General Superintendent is also scheduled to speak at the National Pastors and Leaders Conference, ordain and credential pastors, dedicate a new temple, and hold a high-level strategic meeting with the national leadership of The Gambia Assemblies of God. The Gambia Assemblies of God is the first mission field of the Assemblies of God, Ghana. The church in that country was started by the Assemblies of God, Ghana under the leadership of the late General Superintendent, Rev Simon Asore, about three decades ago. The pioneer National Head of the The Gambia church is Rev (Rtd ) Jerry Adjorlolo. Currently, there are missionaries from the USA Assemblies of God and Brazil working alongside the Ghana Assemblies of God Mission in The Gambia. This is the first time the entire Executive Presbytery officers are visiting The Gambian Assemblies of God Mission. The National Head, Rev Ampofo, expressed great joy at the historic visit, saying, “It will strengthen and advance the mission work in The Gambia.

items.title: Supreme Court ruling on delegate system can help curb ‘moneycracy’ in political parties – Dr Asah-Asante
items.description: Political analyst Dr Kwame Asah-Asante says the Supreme Court’s decision to scrap the delegate system for internal political party elections could help address concerns over the growing influence of money in party politics. According to him, although the implementation of the ruling may come with challenges, it presents an opportunity to improve Ghana’s democratic processes and reduce the excesses associated with “moneycracy”. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Wednesday, August 5, Dr. Asah-Asante said he supports the Supreme Court’s decision, arguing that a broader participation system could help create a fairer internal election process. “I support the Supreme Court ruling because this is one of the surest ways by which we can deal with some of the excesses relative to moneycracy associated with political parties,” he said. He added that the ruling could help “tidy up the whole process for a better kick-off for the democratic process.” Dr. Asah-Asante acknowledged concerns about the financial implications of conducting wider internal party elections but argued that the challenge could be managed through a combination of state support and contributions from political party members. “I belong to that school of thought. I won’t share the view that political party financing must not be brought to the table for discussion. We need that, so as to support a call like this,” he said. He, however, stressed that political parties must also explore ways of financing their own activities rather than relying entirely on public funds. One option, he suggested, is for party members who wish to participate in internal elections to contribute financially towards the process. “Those who are coming to the register can be levied to pay for exercising their rights. I’m not sure it will be a difficult one for people who really want to tell the world that they are members of a certain political party,” he said. Responding to concerns that state funding could give governments undue influence over political parties, Dr. Asah-Asante argued that such fears can be addressed through proper structures and stakeholder involvement. He explained that any funding arrangement should not be controlled by government alone but should involve key stakeholders, including political parties and relevant institutions. “If it’s coming from government, it’s all of us, our contribution. So government cannot control anything,” he said. He proposed that funds meant for internal party elections could be managed through an independent arrangement, with clear guidelines to ensure transparency. “The Electoral Commission can manage as part of their budget, that this is money earmarked for this exercise, and then political parties will add maybe an X amount of money or nothing, then we move on,” he added. Dr. Asah-Asante maintained that with proper safeguards, state support for political party elections could strengthen Ghana’s democracy without compromising the independence of political parties.
